firmwares.title: Official Open
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock). Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: M-VAVE's own open-source firmware, which turns the FM1 into an eight-track groovebox: each track plays a DX7, 303, 808, PSG, Pluck, or sampler engine, with 16 USER project slots and an eight-slot sample bank every project shares. It installs from M-VAVE's FM1 Workbench, which also edits projects, simulates the device, and can put V15 back. This editor recognises it and sends it no Program Change or effect controls, which would change its tracks, but sends it no patches yet: a DX7 track takes a voice or bank downloaded from this editor as a .syx file, through the Workbench. V14 holds 128 independent DX7 voices in four groups of 32 and takes DX7 single-voice and 32-voice bank SysEx. Going back: the Workbench's Restore original V15 replaces all four banks with the factory voices, and a force flash may erase projects and samples, so download a backup from this editor first.

firmwares.title: Stock firmware
firmwares.status: Works with this editor Latest V16 Updated 21 Oct 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The firmware every FM1 ships with: a six-operator FM engine compatible with DX7 voices, four banks of 32 presets, effects, an arpeggiator, and a sequencer. Install it with M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE tool, which is also the way back from Felucca and SLOOP. V16, released on 21 October, makes the FM1 eight-part multitimbral, with 20 voices shared between the parts, longer patterns, and one library of 128 effect settings that every preset shares; this editor has not been tested with it yet. Going back: download the stock firmware from M-VAVE's downloads, under PC Firmware, and install it over whichever firmware the FM1 runs; many custom firmwares' own installers can put it back too. If SLOOP, or a firmware built on it such as sloopDX or zp12, no longer starts, hold OCT− alone while switching the FM1 on: it starts in USB rescue, ready to install again. M-VAVE also publishes a groovebox firmware of its own, Official Open , listed above.

firmwares.title: Baud Girl (FM-1+VA)
firmwares.status: Works with this editor Latest FM-1_102 Updated 19 Oct 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: Keeps M-VAVE's FM engine and effects, fixes its engine bugs, and adds a Virtual Analog engine, an 8-Bit engine, a Bitcrush effect, a 64-step sequencer, and a Note Engine for arpeggios, auto-arpeggios, and auto-chords. It installs from Baud Girl's own browser page, keeps your presets, and can put M-VAVE's firmware back. This editor reads and writes its FM, Virtual Analog, and 8-Bit presets, effects included, keeps the 8-Bit ones in the library, and downloads them as presets files.

firmwares.title: 386DX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Supports Standard MIDI Files (.mid) for compositions.
firmwares.blurb: A karaoke robot with a band, an homage to the performer Alexei Shulgin's 386 DX. It sings songs you bring in from karaoke and MIDI files, and lines you type on the FM1, to the notes you play, with a face whose mouth opens with the sound. Keys, bass, and drums play along with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects. It installs from its own browser page, which also runs it there.

firmwares.title: A22
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An FM workstation derived from h1, with twelve synth and drum engines of eight algorithms each, eight effects, a four-track tape with knob automation, an arpeggiator, and a step sequencer. Its README calls it early: installed and run on one FM1, but not yet played at length by many people. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: ABYSS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental noise synthesiser inspired by the APTBS x Death By Audio Synthesizer, built on felucca-bsp, with three cross-modulating oscillators that offer FM, ring modulation, sync, and chaos. It installs from its release package, with a Python installer or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and has a cheat sheet and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Adrift
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A sixteen-voice physical modelling and virtual analogue synth built around key-tracked bucket-brigade resonators, with morphing oscillators, six multitimbral voice groups each with its own arpeggiator, and a four-stage effects bus. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator and can put M-VAVE’s firmware back.

firmwares.title: AFFINE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A PS1-era jungle break chopper by MONO2K’s maker: royalty-free Amens sliced across the white keys, performance effects held on the black keys, and the sound of a 1990s console’s sound chip, with its reverbs, sample grit, and CD audio. Its README calls 0.3 a beta, tested on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it, or its release package.

firmwares.title: Agent Deck
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a desk controller for coding agents running on a computer, with their states on the key lights and the screen, driven by a program on the computer. Its README says 0.3 runs on its author’s FM1, and 0.6 adds light cues, context gauges, and more sounds. It installs from its release package, plays a scripted session in a browser emulator, and no licence is stated.

firmwares.title: AISLING
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative Irish ambient firmware, a fork of NACHTFAHRT: harps in a jig's threes and a flute over a held drone, in the old modes, with surf, wind, and rain behind. Eight pieces play themselves for ever, and the white keys play a flute that answers you. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator.

firmwares.title: Album
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A series of firmwares, one per record, by Rainbow mode's maker: a few deep sounds drawn from photographs, each moving its photo as it plays. Album 01 bends chords the whole time they ring, through a reverse reverb, with a chord on every key, a soft beat for every patch, and two FM1s playing together over MIDI clock. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: ALTER
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A live euclidean groove machine for industrial techno, noise, and texture, forked from Felucca: three euclidean circles, each playing its own sound from eight engines, driven by dice, chaos, and performance fills instead of a piano keyboard. Its README says 1.0 was tested on an FM1 with the UC25HQ80 flash chip. Version 1.1 adds WAVE, an engine of industrial wavetables. It installs from its own browser page, which has a companion page, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: AMARU OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A hard-tekno generative groovebox built on Bunker Evolved 1.0: pick a genre and a seed, and it writes a 64-step song across four tracks, pad, lead, bass, and drums, the same every time for the same settings. Its README says its song editor’s backup round trip was checked on an FM1. It has no numbered releases: it installs from its own browser page, which writes only over M-VAVE’s V15 or AMARU itself, and has a song editor and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: AMB-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient machine inspired by Brian Eno's Music for Airports. It plays itself from the moment it is switched on: breathing voices, soft bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass, and quiet Euclidean percussion. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: AMB-1 Evolved
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient firmware that keeps AMB-1’s controls, with 64 sounds and 32 themes. Its README, in German, says its maker tried release E1 on their FM1 on 17 October. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: AmbWave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient instrument built on Felucca: four tracks of curated sounds, held chords, scattered notes, and four knobs for Shape, Motion, Density, and Space. It installs from its own web page, with a browser version to try first.

firmwares.title: Amenity
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A live jungle firmware, by Presethead, built on fm1-base. Version 2 adds more breaks, your own breaks and a steadier MIDI clock. It plays the Amen break sliced into sixteen 8ths, with rolls, builds, echoes and an old-sampler stretch on the white keys, single hits on the black keys, a pattern that varies itself and a fill at the end of every phrase, and knobs for a ringing delay, variation, warp and a DJ filter. It installs from its own browser page, and the update loader is included so you can go back to V15.

firmwares.title: ANDROMEDA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient instrument by Polaris Sound Lab, the makers of Dark Funk Durcal Synt, that keeps playing by itself: choose a mood, and on its AUTO page the music keeps growing. The same instrument runs in a browser, as a Mac app, and as an Ableton plug-in, and the FM1's screen reads in English or Spanish. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: April OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca fork for sampling, kept deliberately simple: 32 sample slots of three seconds each, an eight-track sequencer, a sample and loop editor, and recording through a computer's or iPhone's microphone, bridged by its own page. It installs from that page. Its repository holds the page, not the firmware's source.

firmwares.title: AQUORA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient firmware of Solfeggio tones, binaural beats, and soundscapes, with eight musical roles including drums, an eight-track console, and its own AQUORA Sans font. Its 0.7.14 release notes link the firmware package and say testing on a physical FM1 is still pending. Its README says the owner verified 0.2.0 playback on an FM1.

firmwares.title: Araminta
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Felucca 1.5.1 that adds JIANT's DRUM-X drum kit and punch-ins, free-take recording from Sloop, a mixer solo, an effects list you chain or send, and, since 3.0, a WAVETABLE engine. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back.

firmwares.title: Arctic Scream
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A dark ambient drone firmware built on GR!MM, whose new HOWL sound source is a feedback loop that wakes past a threshold and screams. It has 46 factory sounds, six screaming presets, and a browser demo and editor. Version 2.0 adds JIEHKKI, which plays a whole drone piece by itself for 5 to 60 minutes or endlessly, a layer of cracking and dripping ice, pure tunings for drones, and a wind noise source.

firmwares.title: Arcturus S6
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A self-playing wavetable instrument for evolving soundscapes: four PPG-style wavetable oscillators with no sequencer and no filter, moved by Serge-style function generators, sample-and-holds, a quadrature LFO and gate generators, on a Fairlight-style green phosphor screen. Its README says it was written by Claude with human guidance and tested on one FM-1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Argo
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Felucca, formerly called Felucca 8 Patterns, that gives each track eight sequences to swap between and chain one after another, and removes the sampling engines. Its latest release swaps in engines from Mini-Tone and JIANT and adds a preset change on each step. Its repository says a free LLM wrote it. It installs from its own browser page, which also has a web editor.

firmwares.title: ARP WAV 09
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A minimal firmware with no menus and no sound presets, played with the knobs: six voices to play alone or chained together, an arpeggiator, a WAV drone, a sequencer, KIT drums, X02 ghost and alien noises, and A09 ghost radio. It is built on Dinghy, installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: ARPHONY
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A modal arpeggiator firmware that plays riffs over slowly moving modal chords, with a bass note and up to two chord tones. It is built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open. It installs from its own browser page or the release package. Its README says it was tested on one FM-1 unit; no licence is stated.

firmwares.title: ARTIHIVE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-voice drone and polyphonic synthesiser. Its README says it has had only limited testing on physical FM1 hardware, and that 2.0.2 removed repeated high-contrast flashing from 2.0.1's DISORDER mode. It comes with an install page and manuals in English and Russian.

firmwares.title: ASTRA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Works out the positions of the Sun, Moon, and planets on the FM1 itself and turns a birth chart into an FM patch: ten operators, one for each body, wired by the aspects between them, so the sound moves as the sky does. The screen also reads the day's transits. Its README says it installs and works on a physical FM1 and is still an early build. Its site installs it and runs the firmware in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: ATEK303
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Animatek's firmware for the FM1, named for the TB-303, kept in a repository that also holds notes on the platform, written in Spanish. It installs from the atek303-1.1.fwsc package in its release.

firmwares.title: Atl-Atl
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A USB audio interface and autotuner on FM1_AudioBase: play computer audio into it and hold a key to tune it, with a three-second sampler, tempo, an arpeggiator mask, and latch. Its README says it has been installed and updated on a real FM1, and calls the autotuner a work in progress. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: B1 Drawbar Organ
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drawbar organ, by BEETLE's maker. Its README says B1 has been installed and tested on a real FM1, including booting and sound output, and its release package comes with a browser installer.

firmwares.title: B3 ORGAN
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A B3 tonewheel organ worked out from setBfree's own data: 91 tonewheels, nine drawbars, key click, vibrato and chorus, percussion, overdrive, reverb, and a Leslie, with all 110 of setBfree's programs. Its README says 0.2 has been tested on an FM1 by one person. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser, and since 0.5 has a web editor that reads and writes the FM1.

firmwares.title: BAILE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Brazilian rhythm kits by Mulú: Tamborzão, Voltmix, and Beat Bolha, with 12 samples built in and a 16-step bar for each preset. Its README calls 0.7 stable after a user reported it working on their FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: BAILE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A tracker for Brazilian funk by Coqui’s maker: six tracks, a step sequencer whose patterns chain into a song, and 64 live effects, with tamborzão, Volt Mix, and montagem among its styles. Its site and notes are in Portuguese. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator and a manual.

firmwares.title: Bass Something 2
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock).
firmwares.blurb: A monosynth firmware in the style of the Bass Station 2, with 32 factory patches of its own and Bass Station II patch dumps in and out over SysEx. It also works from an iPhone or iPad in RemoteFM1, and from 0.8.1 plays through Bluetooth headphones and speakers. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: BBL JAM BOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A live-jamming groovebox in the style of the Digitone and Model:Cycles, modified from Felucca. It has six tracks with 16-step sequencers, parameter locks, a four-operator FM engine, 808-style drums, and a sampler for your own sounds, and installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: BEETLE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A six-lane tracker and drum machine: five synth lanes and a drum lane, 48 patterns, songs, and live effects, played from the FM1's own controls, with six channels of USB audio out. It installs from its own browser page, beside a simulator and a project manager.

firmwares.title: BEETLE BLUE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: The drum-focused fork of BEETLE: a six-lane drum tracker with two built-in ROM drum engines, 48 patterns of 1 to 16 steps per lane, a song mode of up to 64 positions, and a live mode with a 24-position setlist. Its README says the developer tested it on two FM1s. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Beiwagen
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Makes the FM1 a USB sidecar for the teenage engineering OP-1 Field: the OP-1 streams its four tape tracks to the FM1, and the FM1 sends a chosen pair back as the OP-1’s USB input to record. Its README says this was tested with an OP-1 Field on firmware 1.7.3, and lists what is built but not yet tested. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package.

firmwares.title: Berlinan
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative sequencer in the Berlin School tradition, for the FM1 to run on its own. A small ensemble of voices repeat and phase against each other on loops of unequal length, each going out on its own MIDI channel over USB, as the FM1 makes no sound of its own. It plays what Berlinan for macOS plays and installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Big Beat Studio BB1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Big Beat Studio BB1 2.0, built on Felucca: two independent drum layers and Dillo acid bass, sharing tape echo and spring reverb. A synthesised 808 and seven sampled machines, 539 rhythm sections including 138 Roland rhythms, and 205 acid bass phrases. Version 2.0 adds a song arranger, ratchets, reversible Evolve, swung recording, a kit builder and 31 additional drum kits. Use its own installer for the application and matched sound library. Release notes document the known audio timing limitation.

firmwares.title: Big Beat Studio BB-BOB
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Western swing bandstand in your FM1. Call one of 50 classics or hit New Tune and see what the band comes up with, give Leon the steel break, throw in a fill, and bring them back to the theme. Turn Then/Now and the rhythm section picks up acid bass and electronic drums. BB-BOB is standalone FM1 firmware. The product page has the current install instructions.

firmwares.title: Bigorna
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware for rhythmic noise, power noise, industrial, and IDM, after the Elektron Digitone II. It installs from its own browser page, and its manual is on the same site.

firmwares.title: Bloomy
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track firmware with its site and manual in Italian. Its 1.3.4 gives the Knit tracks two oscillators with their own filters and envelopes and a chorus on each Knit and Jacquard track, with five project slots. It has no GitHub release; it installs from its own browser page, which also has tools for backups, loading and saving songs, converting projects, and exporting audio, with an emulator and a PDF manual. Its README says the new functions of 1.3.4 have no documented hardware test yet.

firmwares.title: Blues Box
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A 12-bar and 8-bar blues backing band with 14 grooves, 14 bass engines, 18 keyboard tones, and 12 drum kits, separate fullness and variation controls, live cues, 16 preset slots on the white keys, and a four-voice lead synth whose lights show the chord root and the blues scale. Its README says it was built and tested on the original FM1. It installs from its own browser page, with builds for the SMK-37 keyboards too.

firmwares.title: Boardwalk
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A seaside arcade of music games for the FM1: cabinets such as Striker, Moles, Tiles, Gull and Teacups pay out tickets that trade for prizes. It installs from its own browser page or from its release package, and can be tried in a browser emulator first. The README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.

firmwares.title: bocjuhn
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental six-track instrument with eight sound engines, free loops, and clock. It is a fork, and its README says RC7 was tested on the owner's FM1 and is confirmed working, with a hardware test record in the repository. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: BONBLOOP
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP 2.8.5 with a synth mode added: holding ENV turns the selected track into a three-oscillator synth with ten wavetables, an envelope and an LFO for each oscillator, a filter, and an effects chain you build. It also adds chord voicings and more delay times. It installs from its own browser page, and its guide is in Portuguese.

firmwares.title: Bongo Cat’s Tiny Studio
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A playable little band built on Felucca 1.6.1: a cat plays the keys while three more react to the music, with thirteen sound engines, a generated backing band, and a looper for your own melodies. Its README says the upgrade from 0.3.0 to this release candidate was tested on one FM1. It installs through Felucca's updater from its release package.

firmwares.title: BoopBox
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A renamed fork of SLOOP that carries on from SLOOP 2.8.3 with an eight-track project format of its own. Since 14 Nov its site, installer, and web editor are on Replit. It installs from its own browser page, which also updates an FM1 running SLOOP or Felucca, and has a web editor.

firmwares.title: BOP-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A music toy for children that is also a real synthesizer: every control is a friend whose body is the sound, and the same toy grows from pressing things at three, to beats and loops, to a subtractive synth with its real names. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first and printable guides.

firmwares.title: BOURDON
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone instrument, called DR1 until 0.33: three voices with styles and free frequencies, links between the voices, a mixer, and effects. Its README calls it early work, tested on one FM1, and it installs from its release package with a Python tool on a Mac or Linux.

firmwares.title: Braindancer
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An IDM and braindance firmware, a fork of JIANT FM, formerly called ACID FM. Its 0.9.1, the version its README names, trims JIANT's engines for IDM, gives its sound, sequencer, global and MIDI screens an acid look of its own, and has a generator that writes whole songs on the device across its genres; breakbeats loaded from its web page are planned. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: BRUSSELS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox by Piknik Elektronik, built on JIANT and Felucca and drawn in Brussels: an MS-20-style analogue engine, FM, a lo-fi chip engine, a synthesised drum kit, a 64-step sequencer, and drawings of its own that move with the music. Its site, in French and English, installs it, and has a browser emulator and a web editor.

firmwares.title: BRUTAL FM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An FM synth for industrial techno, noise, and dark ambient, built on Felucca: four operators in a 4×4 modulation matrix, METAL, GROWL, CHAOS, and NOISE modes, a wavefolder, a morph between two sounds, and a COMPLEX ARP that generates a pattern from the keys held and keeps it as a loop. Its README, in Japanese, says it runs on an FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Bubba Machine
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track live groovebox written from scratch. Since 0.10 its HOME is a six-channel mixer, and entering a channel hands the FM1 to its machine, laid out like the real one: a TB-303, a Minimoog, a Juno-6, Vital, and the FM1's own DX7-style synth, with drums on a step sequencer of their own and the BP-1 Slicer for your recordings. It installs from a browser page and has been tested on one FM1. Until 1.0 an update can erase what you saved: 0.10 clears saved patterns and scenes once on its first start, keeping takes and settings. Its documentation is in Spanish and English.

firmwares.title: Bunker Evolved
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Kid Bunka's generative ambient firmware, a Felucca fork with four editable layers, 64 sounds, 24 worlds, and GROW, which varies the scale. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser first, and has an editor for Chrome.

firmwares.title: Burger Studio FM-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A sampling-first firmware built on Felucca 1.8.2: its Firmware Hub card says a SAMPLE row on HOME opens a page to trim and slice the three user sample slots, and that one sample can span two or three of them. Its 1.8.2-bs19 release makes track 5 the sample track, with a guitar-style looper and a ROCK LIVE drum kit. The release notes call it a beta and say to back up first, and its README is still Felucca’s. It installs from its release package and has a browser editor.

firmwares.title: Bytemania
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A bytebeat synth built on Dinghy: the note you play sets how fast a formula of t runs, and the knobs change the numbers inside it. It has 30 built-in patches, 64 user slots, a live formula compiler on the device, and a random formula generator. It comes as a release package, not a page that installs it.

firmwares.title: Caravel
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A multi-engine synthesiser, an independent fork of Felucca 1.6.1 continued now that Felucca's own development has ended, with SEM, HADES, and DRONE among its engines and screen colours of your own set from its web editor. Version 1.0 starts afresh: backups from before 1.0 are not imported, and the 0.13 line is no longer maintained. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Carnac OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A wavetable synth themed on Carnac's standing stones: 15 morphing wavetable banks, seven voice architectures, among them STRIKE with 20 synthesised Neolithic attack sounds, four filter types, spring, tomb, and tank reverbs, a step sequencer, an arpeggiator, and two layers with splits. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in fm1-emu.

firmwares.title: Castletunia
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A generative dungeon-synth and 16-bit RPG soundtrack on Dinghy, by Blues Box’s maker. Phrases played on the keys become a party’s attacks on a boss, woven into a four-bar arrangement with chords and drums across nine pixel-art stages, while the boss answers with counter-attacks that change the music. Its README says it was built and tested on an FM1, and it installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: CHAOS MACHINE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Four generators, circuit, machine, organism, and radio, each with 30 synthesised sounds, that play by themselves and can be played from the keys. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which says it still needs testing on an FM1.

firmwares.title: Chipbox
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Chiptune music on the FM1: build songs from NES, Game Boy and Master System sound chips, then wreck them with punch-in effects. It comes with the Tetris theme preloaded and plenty of free space for your own, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried first in a browser.

firmwares.title: CHOPPAH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A breakbeat chopper: a break is cut into sixteen slices on the white keys, with momentary effect pads, a generator that rearranges the break and a master effects chain. Eight classic breaks are built in, and there are sixteen patterns with a step sequencer and a synthesised kick, snare and hat on the drum lanes. The README says the engine, slicer, pads, generator and effects work on the device. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and the installer can put M-VAVE's firmware back.

firmwares.title: ChoralRoot
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord instrument inspired by Telepathic Instruments' Orchid: one hand plays roots while the other shapes chords, with voicings, key and performance modes, a bass line, and a looper. Built on Felucca's engines and the monome grid ChoralRoot, it installs from its own browser page and can be tried first in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: ChoralRoot J-6
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Quixotic7's ChoralRoot FM-1 that adds 100 chord sets in the style of the Roland AIRA J-6, with a ready-made chord for each of the twelve notes. It installs from its own browser page or its release package. Its README says it was written entirely by an AI and has not been run on a real FM1, only in tests and an emulator.

firmwares.title: CHORD RUN
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A one-finger chord player based on Blop: a song’s chords sit on the black keys and a scale-matched melody on the white keys, across 17 songs with their own sounds and drums, thirteen drum styles, and a four-bar looper, while a runner runs as long as you play, with missions and characters to unlock. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: CHRISTMAS MACHINE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: Plays 36 traditional carols in full instrumental arrangements, about an hour of them, with a melody of recorded grand piano or flute samples since 0.4, in four voices to choose from, and an organ to play along on the keys. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which says it still needs testing on an FM1.

firmwares.title: CLATTER Pocket
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: CLATTER's LXR-02 drum synthesis as a generative drum machine: seven voices, a 64-step sequencer with conditions and per-step pitch, patterns generated and mutated in 11 styles, and nine named projects. Its README says 1.0.0 was hardware verified on one FM1, installed from stock V15 and over earlier firmware, and that Bluetooth, DIN MIDI, and SAFE MODE are untested. It installs from a browser installer, with a demo to try first.

firmwares.title: Clavioline
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A recreation of the 1947 Clavioline, an early electronic analogue synthesiser, rebuilt on Dinghy from the original circuit diagrams, with its tone-shaping stops, vibrato, and knee-lever expression. It installs from its release package or through the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in fm1-emu in a browser.

firmwares.title: Clipper
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A synthesizer from SLOOP, and so from Felucca, with 23 engines and 407 sounds in one instrument and no tracks, drum machine, or song mode. Among them are a three-oscillator voice, a six-operator FM engine that also plays the DX7 voices of a bank, and wavetables. Its notes call it experimental and say it has run very little on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page, with a web editor.

firmwares.title: COLLAPSE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A physics drum machine, by SIX MACHINES’ maker, inspired by the 3D physics synth Anukari: six synthesised instruments hang in a web of springs, so each hit shoves its neighbours and no two hits sound the same. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Compás
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A Latin rhythm section for cumbia, salsa, merengue and bolero: cue the next section and the band lands on it together. It has 38 groove studies, each naming its source, in 4/4, 6/8 and 12/8, a KUMBIA page with the Hanan Cumbia drum machine's sounds, a TR-727 percussion mode, and screens in English or Spanish. Shows and user rhythms survive power-off but not a firmware update, so export them with its browser editor first. The browser player needs nothing.

firmwares.title: CONCRÈTE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Four found-sound processes that move across the stereo field, with a dark drone on the keys, a shimmer reverb, and a filtered static wind. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which keeps its earlier versions for going back.

firmwares.title: CONDUCTOR
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A pocket symphony orchestra groovebox built on Dinghy, by Clavioline’s maker, with strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion: compose in a piano roll or in notation, conduct each section with articulations, dynamics, and expression curves, and arrange patterns into whole pieces. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in fm1-emu in a browser.

firmwares.title: Coqui
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Latin and Caribbean groovebox: congas, bongos, timbales, güiro, clave and cowbell synthesised on the FM1, played by hand or by the sequencer, with a HUMAN knob that loosens the hand. Its README says 1.0 was tested on a real FM1, installed from the official V15 and from another firmware. It installs from its release package and has a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: CoralFlower
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord instrument inspired by Telepathic Instruments' Orchid: press a chord key and each note you play becomes a whole chord, with a bass underneath, while a pixel flower grows from your chords. It installs from its own browser page, which saves your sounds first when the FM1 runs CoralFlower, ChoralRoot, or Felucca, and a browser version plays it first.

firmwares.title: CORD
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord instrument, groovebox, and songwriting companion: choose a progression and a sound, press PLAY, then add drums, shape the bass, turn a chord into an arpeggio, or take over with your own playing, with a live chord display on the home screen. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: CORTEX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Supports Standard MIDI Files (.mid) for compositions.
firmwares.blurb: A generative FM instrument forked from AMB-1: three six-operator FM voices with DX7 banks play chords that grow by themselves, a tape reel records and replays them, songs come in from MIDI files, and a video synth on the screen moves with the music, while a cartoon cat explains each page. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page and plays in a browser simulator first.

firmwares.title: COSMOS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone synthesiser played by the sky: two drones that never stop, shaped by the sun’s height, the clouds, the air pressure, geomagnetic activity, and the moon’s phase, with the screen showing the sky over your location. Its README names version 1.0. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser on a simulated FM1.

firmwares.title: COWBELL
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A cowbell machine after Bad Gear's Volca Cowbell joke, built on M-VAVE's open SDK: a giant MORE knob for ratchets, FEVER for pitch, and PRESCRIPTION choosing one of 13 cowbells sampled from a TR-8S and a DM-10. It installs from its release package with a command-line installer, and a browser page sends the full-quality samples.

firmwares.title: Crepuscular Homunculus
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A synth and four-track groovebox, called TERKINSTEIN until 0.26. It plays, edits, sequences, and saves on the FM1 itself, with piano-roll editing, saved song swing, and a virtual FM1 to try in a browser. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Croc-O-Synth
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A synth for children, built on fm1-base: a crocodile teaches synth basics one lesson per button, with three croc sizes, presets, and a croc to name. Its README says it runs on a real FM1. Its release holds a development build, replaced on every build, and it plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: CRT-4
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-track groovebox that plays the sound chips of nine game consoles and home computers, with drums on the first track and sixteen sounds per console on the others. The screen is themed to the chosen console. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser emulator lets you try it without an FM1.

firmwares.title: CS-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Yamaha CS-80 in the FM1: two channels a voice, the CS-80's own preset tones, a ribbon on the SELECT knob, and a plate reverb that goes on for ever. It is built to be played from a sequencer through the TRS jack, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried first in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: CULTBOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A three-channel machine for drums, a Polivoks-style synth and a dub siren, each with its own sequencer and effects: ten Elka Drummer One samples with a 16 to 64 step sequencer, a duophonic voice with an arpeggiator and a recordable note sequencer, and a siren after dubmarine. Two BBD-style echoes and a per-channel pan finish the mix. It runs on the FM1 by itself, plays in a browser, and its package accepts both flash chips found in FM1 units. A fork of Dinghy.

firmwares.title: CTL-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a MIDI controller: the keys play in a scale with its chords under the black keys, four banks of knobs send controllers, and an arpeggiator and a four-track Euclidean drum sequencer run on its clock. It plays General MIDI sounds of its own too, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried first in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: cursed os
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox on JIANT FM's engines and sequencer, with an Elektron-style interface: one-press loops in five styles, generators for 303 lines, dub chords, and Euclidean rhythms, parameter locks and trig conditions, and the FM1 following an Elektron Syntakt's clock and patterns. Its README calls it early: it runs on its author's FM1 and has not been tried on many units. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Cut-A-Dor
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: Kid Bunka's beat machine: 64 drum one-shots and 12 break arrangements, three expansion banks of recorded hits, and eight punches you can record. It installs from its own browser page, which also covers recovery, and a browser editor plays it first.

firmwares.title: CYMA-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A playable Chladni plate: keys strike, bow or rain on a virtual metal plate, and the sand on the screen settles into the figure you hear, using modal synthesis. It installs from its release package (cyma-1-v1.1.3.fwsc). The README says it has run on a real FM1 since 2026-10-29.

firmwares.title: DABKE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An Arabic wedding keyboard by STUDIOMORPHIK: maqam scales with quarter tones on any note, dabke and shaabi rhythms, mijwiz, zurna, oud, and qanun voices, a drone, and eight tracks with loops and steps, where leaning on a key bends the note. Its README calls it a public beta, tested on one FM1 with the newer flash chip. It installs from its own browser page, and has a manual and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Dark Funk Durcal Synt
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox for acid, breaks, jungle, and warped funk that is always in key: blend two of 15 styles and SUMMON plays drums, acid, bass, and melody at once, with eight live pads for mutes, fills, builds, and drops. The same instrument plays in a browser and as a free plugin, and the FM1's screen reads in English or Spanish. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: DARK-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A dark-music firmware modified from PERF-1, with 16 dark genres, 160 factory pieces and a Wander mode that evolves the music by itself. It installs from its release package with an FM-1 installer page, and can be played in a browser first. The README says it was installed and tried on one real FM-1 by its author.

firmwares.title: Daurade
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware that plays a groove when you press PLAY: a filtered loop, a mix that ducks on each kick, a robot voice and drums, in ten styles steered with four knobs. It is built on Tuna and Felucca. It installs from its own browser page over USB, and can be tried in a browser first. It runs on the FM-1, with no warranty.

firmwares.title: DAYV-X
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Felucca 1.8.2 with hazy, slightly detuned synths, dusty synthesised drums, and a tape stage over the whole mix, with no samples of its own: it adds a DRIFT engine, AGE for tape wear and hiss, and a DUST drum kit. Its README says it has run on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: DEEP FIELD
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient drone machine on fm1-base: every key swells in a voice that stays, eight of them drawn as beams on the screen, and GEN moves them through a chord progression or a Euclidean arpeggio by themselves. It has thirteen models, a noise layer, a hall reverb with freeze and shimmer, a delay, and 32 presets. Its notes say an update was confirmed on hardware. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator.

firmwares.title: Del Rio
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A rhythm box of hand percussion for accompanying songs in a circle: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas, and triangle, with their strokes on the black keys and a step sequencer on the white, and a berimbau and tanpura and shruti box drones played on their own. Built on fm1-base, it installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Demake synth
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient lo-fi machine, by MONO2K's maker, built on 64 recordings made with pedals and played by three synths, each with its own piano roll, patterns, and chain of lo-fi effects, with scenes, a song, and a chord machine leading them. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: DIRGE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: Darksynth, noise, and drone firmware built on Felucca 1.6.1: four tracks, fifteen engines among them its own DRONE and BASS, a 64-step sequencer per track with chords, ratchets, conditions, and parameter locks, an arpeggiator, a song chain, and MIDI clock in, under long, worn effects. It installs from its own browser page, plays the real firmware in a browser, and has a web editor for sounds, samples, and backups.

firmwares.title: DFD ACID ENGINE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Acid and dirty electro on one squelching voice, playing 16-step riffs from its web generator, with 16 styles, 19 sounds, and a DIRTY page of distortion and pumping. It shares its patterns with its browser and plug-in versions, its README marks the FM1 edition as tested on hardware, and it installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Dinghy
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The smallest firmware to build your own on, by sloopDX's author. It plays a sine wave on the keys and nothing more; under it, the update path, USB rescue, USB MIDI and audio, the panel, the screen, and settings all work and are documented. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: DØG-5
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An aggressive virtual-analogue synth made for the band DØGS: eight voices through a chain of GROWL, ALLEY, DRAIN, and CHEW, with 99 program slots and 32 factory patches. Its README says it has been tested on one FM1 with the older flash chip, and never installed on one with the newer chip. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Doom (E1M1)
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: Doom as the FM1's firmware, separate from FM-1 Doom. It has been installed and played on one FM1, replaces the synth firmware, and installs from its own browser page, which fetches the shareware game data into your browser.

firmwares.title: Double Rainbow
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Rainbow mode's older sibling, for ages ten and up, built on Melodee: 30 characters escaped from the Keeper's jars, each a real synth engine, from a Prophet-5 and FM to a TB-303 and an 808. Each has four knobs, a beat, an arp, and codex pages on its engine, with chord modes, an ear trainer, and 14 songs to learn one key at a time. Holding HOME and SAVE opens the full Melodee synth. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: DP3OYB
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track performance groovebox grown from Felucca, adding two LFOs with sequencer trigs, retriggering envelopes, a mixer and a track sequencing view with quick-access controls, and note hold across tracks. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: DRIFT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient instrument based on Felucca: classic synth sounds, basses, pads, and plucks on two oscillators with three sample slots, under a repeating generative Euclidean sequencer, in a minimal monochrome interface. Its README says earlier builds were tested by users and that 0.9.6 itself still needs a test on a real FM1. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Drum Peter
firmwares.status: Beta · No numbered releases Updated 26 Nov 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine with 808, 909, 606, and 707 kits on four tracks, eight songs ready to play, and TR-style step keys, on a two-tone phone-style screen whose button lights blink to show what is happening. Its README calls it a beta, tested on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE’s V15 back.

firmwares.title: Drumlab
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine after Microtonic, built on Chipbox: 16 sounds, 16 patterns, and four lanes, with Microtonic presets and patterns brought in on its projects page, and kits and patterns sent to a Teenage Engineering PO-32. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: Drumtonic
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine of ten synthesised drum channels, with no samples: 32 patterns of up to 64 steps with parameter locks, conditions, micro timing and ratchets, free recording, beat repeat, eight LFOs a pattern, and a reverb, tape delay, and compressor. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: DUB-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative dub techno machine, a fork of AMB-1. It plays itself from the moment it is switched on: chord stabs through a resonant low-pass into a tape echo, FM pings on loops of unequal length, a sub bass, a four-on-the-floor kick, and vinyl crackle. You steer it rather than play it. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Doom FM-1 / SMK
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A Doom-engine port for the FM-1 and the SMK-37 Pro and Elite, with the nine original maps and three weapons. Its page builds the right firmware for your model and installs it over USB from a browser, and can play it there first. It replaces the synth application, and its page says to back up your projects first. Release 26 for the FM-1 moves the controls to the GameDude layout; the SMK-37 build stays on release 24.

firmwares.title: DUB-BOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: FM-1 Audio Router, the FM1's USB sound card and Bluetooth receiver, with SLOOP Dub's dub modules on top: a DJ filter, a siren, a tape echo, and an isolator, each on its own page, over whatever you feed it from a computer, a phone, or a mixer. It has no sequencer and no synths. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser emulator first.

firmwares.title: dubengine
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Two tracks of dub chords, a bass, and an FM ping, for dub techno, minimal, and microhouse, with one-finger chords in root position or either inversion. It has no GitHub release; it installs from its own browser page, which can also put the stock firmware back, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: DUELL
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A multimorphing bitimbral synth built on Felucca: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines with wavetables, twin filters, effects, and a mod matrix, with macros, velocity, aftertouch, and MIDI presets for Circuit Tracks and MPC or Force. It has run on its author’s two FM-1 units. It installs from its own browser page, has a web editor and a cheat sheet, and plays in a browser emulator first.

firmwares.title: Dungeon Tracker
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A tracker-style four-track FM groovebox forked from Felucca 1.6.1, with a first-person dungeon crawl on its home screen that the song plays. It adds FM drum and tone engines, wavetable and SID-style voices, and new drum kits. It installs from its release package (.fwsc).

firmwares.title: DUODRONE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A two-stylus drone synth after the Dubreq Stylophone CPM DS-2, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page, which also offers a USB rescue and the way back to M-VAVE's firmware.

firmwares.title: DX747
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-part multitimbral DX7 module. Every part has its own MIDI channel and up to eight layered DX7 voices, with key splits, velocity windows, 64 scenes, a master filter, and shared reverb and delay, and it imports DX7 ROMs. It has no sequencer, sampler, or projects. It is a fork of Official Open, so it brings M-VAVE's update loader, and it installs from its own page over Web MIDI in Chrome or Edge. It can be tried in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Echo Ludwig
firmwares.status: Experimental · No numbered releases Updated 26 Nov 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A listening game for blind and low-vision players: hear a melody, play it back, and watch it grow, through 25 public-domain classics remixed as chiptune, house, trance, and techno. A small built-in speech synth reads the menus aloud. Its README calls these first builds experimental, and it keeps its progress in project slot 15.

firmwares.title: ECHOFIELD
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A free, open-source granular sampler: a few seconds of any sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells, played from the FM1's keys and knobs in six modes (CLOUD, DUST, TAPE, BLOOM, PULSE and DRIFT). Its grains render across both cores, and 0.2.9 follows MIDI clock. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Elixir
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The Erica Synths LXR-02 drum machine's sound engine and sequencer on the FM1, formerly called Kettle: six voices on seven tracks, 32 patterns with parameter locks, songs, kits, and projects, and MIDI in and out with clock sync. Version 1.0 adds new sound engines, a rebuilt effects section and recording over USB. It is unofficial, and not affiliated with Erica Synths or M-VAVE. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a browser, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: Emerald YM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative 16-bit music firmware with a YM2612 FM sound, Sega-style PSG voices, live keys, and per-instrument effects. Its release notes call 1.0.4 a stable release, retested on an FM1, and it installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: ENJAMBRE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: Felucca with a new engine, ENJAMB, in which insects move as agents through an orbital, quantum or atomic field, so that playing a note collapses or excites the swarm. Its pages are in Spanish. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a browser, and has a web editor.

firmwares.title: Entropy Helios
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-voice ambient drone and microtonal synthesiser on fm1-base: six swarm drone voices and two melodic voices through two filters, a spring tank, and sixteen effects that stack, with 36 presets and eight user slots. It can process USB audio coming in, and has a WebMIDI studio page. Its README says the 1.3.1 beta supports both FM1 flash chips. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: ESTAMPIE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A mediæval groovebox for lively tavern and court dances: plucked lutes and citoles, hurdy-gurdies, shawms, and bagpipes over drones, frame drums, and chant, in the mediæval modes. It started as a fork of GHOULBOX, itself a Felucca fork. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first, and since 0.3.0 it can tell a screen reader what its screen shows.

firmwares.title: ETCH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A synth you draw, morph, and modulate. It installs from its own web page and comes as a .fwsc package. Its README calls it an experimental build and says that installing it, and returning from it to other firmware, has not been verified on real FM1 hardware.

firmwares.title: Evander's Music Box
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A bard's synthesiser for live-action role play, with medieval and high-fantasy sounds. Its README says it is in early hardware testing. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator and a manual.

firmwares.title: EVIL GENIUS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A SID chip groovebox that talks, built on FIZZ by its maker: six tracks of C64 SID voices and SAM speech, per-step sound locks, conditions, ratchets, MIDI effects, and a tower of eight retro effects with a send for each track, with Bluetooth MIDI and USB audio. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a browser and manages its sounds.

firmwares.title: Fantasma
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient firmware forked from Felucca, which keeps all of its engines and adds a Pad that writes its own chords, bells that play themselves, an endless noise engine of sea, rain, or vinyl, and an Omnichord on the keys. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Fart Machine One
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A joke instrument that plays: eleven “artisanal farts” on the keys, a reverb, a delay, and a 16-step sequencer, with a loop you record and hear back, which switching the FM1 off clears. There is no browser installer: you download the package and its source, then install with a Python tool from a terminal.

firmwares.title: Felucca
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a multi-engine synth: thirteen engines, from analogue, six-operator FM, and phase distortion to samples, granular, drums, and physical models from Mutable Instruments' Plaits and Rings, across four tracks with a 64-step sequencer, arpeggiator, and modulation matrix. It has its own web editor and installer, and 1.8.2 supports newer FM1s with the UC25HQ80 flash chip.

firmwares.title: Felucca [Salt]
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca fork with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser, which plays without an FM1 or edits the one connected. It installs from its own browser page and leaves through M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE.

firmwares.title: Felucca MPE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Felucca 1.6.1 that adds MPE support, a per-voice LFO and a DRIFT source for chords that move and breathe. It installs from the .fwsc package committed in the repository. Its README says it has only been tried in the browser emulator and never installed on a real FM-1.

firmwares.title: Fernbedienung
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a controller and USB audio interface for Steckfeld SF1, a modular synth app for iPad and iPhone: the keys play it, the knobs and buttons edit it, and the screen shows the selected module. Its 1.2 release needs Steckfeld SF1 1.7.0 or newer. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package.

firmwares.title: FIELD
firmwares.status: Alpha · No numbered releases Updated 26 Oct 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A field-recording radio powered by Radio Aporee, over the FM1's Wi-Fi: choose a country or region on a globe and listen, then capture a few seconds into a lo-fi sampler that plays on the keys, loops, and slices. Its README says the first alpha was reported working on an FM1, and that 0.1.19, which its installer page offers, still needs a test on one.

firmwares.title: FIENDBOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A demon synth for dark, occult music, from old JRPG dungeons to dungeon synth: a GHOULBOX fork, itself built on Felucca, with ideas and code from JIANT FM. It adds five power-on scenes, a creature drawn for each engine on its edit pages, and bytebeat and floatbeat waves for the LOFI engine. Its README says it has been tested on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page and has a web editor.

firmwares.title: FiMba-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A kalimba grown from FoMni: the 16 white keys are tines laid out as a real kalimba's, each a physical model of a metal, bamboo, or glass bar on a body of your choosing, and the 11 black keys play thumb-roll chords, with mbira patterns, a granular cloud, delay, reverb, and tape. Its own page installs it and plays it in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Finton
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track trance machine after Rollwerk: kick, 909 kit, bass, roller, lead, and pad play over a library of 66 chord progressions, with parameter locks and one knob, LIFT, that runs the build and the drop. It installs from its own browser flasher.

firmwares.title: FIZZ
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A step-sequencer groovebox for ChoralRoot's FM TONE voice: tracks sharing a pool of sounds, a 64-step grid with microtiming, parameter locks, conditions, chance, ratchets and chords, Euclidean and grid generators, and a web sound editor and manager. Version 0.12.0, its first release out of beta, lets the FM1's USB port host a USB-MIDI keyboard or synth, with a powered hub. Its own page plays a preview in the browser and installs it over USB.

firmwares.title: FLAT-20
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A circuit-level model of the Korg MS-20, built on Dinghy from the part values in its service manual: the KORG35 filters are solved sample by sample, with the MS-20’s Hz/V pitch and switch triggers. Its README says 0.2 was tested on hardware, and that all 16 factory presets were recorded from an FM1. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: Flyfish
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: One piece on the FM1: Chopin's Étude Op. 10 No. 1 on a sampled Steinway D, to play, shape, and practise, built on Tuna and Felucca. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Again
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: Warm, rhythmic electronic music by Arctic Scream’s maker: eight grooves with their own swing, four chord progressions in any key, and a soft FM electric piano, sung syllables, and a chopped recording of your own on the keys, with build-ups and drops, eleven performance pads, and a song mode that plays a whole 72-bar track by itself. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE’s firmware back, plays in a browser, and has an editor for every value.

firmwares.title: FM-1 ZX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A ZX Spectrum 48K emulator that plays Spectrum games with the FM1’s keys and knobs, replacing the beeper’s sounds with FM instruments as they play. Five freely licensed games are built in, a tool packs your own, and a paused game survives a power cycle. Its README says it runs and is tested on an FM1; it installs from its release package and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: FM ARCAVE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A music game played with the knobs and keys: wake up Rock, roll down to the cave, and mend a jukebox with a song of your own, then play three arcade machines. Its README says its first two releases were installed and played on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page and plays in an emulator.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Audio Router
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a two-in, two-out USB audio interface and a Bluetooth audio receiver with SBC, AAC, aptX and aptX HD, with a mixer, a five-band EQ, a peak limiter, and meters, waveforms and a spectrum on the screen. It installs with M-Flasher once the m-bootloader has been flashed, rather than from a browser page.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Chimera Vocal
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A singing human voice, ported from Jameson Hodge’s CHIMERA and built on fm1-base: a simulated airway of lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth, and nose sings words a syllable a key, or holds vowels shaped with the knobs, and the words are written in a browser Studio and sent over USB. It installs from its own browser page, and has a manual and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Ear Trainer
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: An ear-training game on Melodee: it plays one to four hidden notes in C major or A minor, in one octave or across the keyboard, and you find them on the keys, with current and best ratings saved for each mode and FM6 or Prophet sounds. Since 0.0.16 it also has a metronome with tap tempo and rhythm games that score your timing. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a guide.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Midi-Mania
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A rhythm game built on Felucca: load a MIDI file in the browser Studio, and your part’s notes fall to the keys while the FM1 plays the rest on its synth engines. You play keys, drums, guitar, or bass, with every note judged, combos, and best scores. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: FM-1 SID
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Joakim Eriksson's SID synth for the FM1, which plays C64 tunes and GoatTracker songs and lets you write music with the GoatTracker editor. It runs on fm1-dock, and its README says it has played on an FM1.

firmwares.title: FM-FAM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A drum synth and 16-step sequencer in the style of the DFAM: two oscillators with 16 wave types, a kick with its own sequencer, parameter locks, a sound saved with each pattern, effects, scales, presets, and projects. It installs from its release package, and its screen mirror page shows and plays the FM1's panel from a computer.

firmwares.title: FM-KICK
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A kick drum synthesiser with a sequencer of up to 32 steps, built on fm1-base: seven kinds of kick, from 808 and 909 to FM and a wave shaper, with 48 parameters, effects held on the keys, a master chain, parameter locks, a condition and a chance on every step, nine generators, and four LFOs. Its README calls it beta. It installs from its release package, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FM1 Pocket Tutor
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A study firmware on fm1-dock: the keys light up to show where to play while a lesson page in Chrome guides notes, scales, chords, and the chord progressions of songs, section by section, with six-operator FM sounds. Its notes are in Portuguese and English. Since 0.7 it installs from its own browser page, or from its release package through the FM-1 Firmware Hub or a command-line installer.

firmwares.title: FM1 SMSGGDJ
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: The Game Gear tracker SMSGGDJ on the FM1: a Game Gear emulator boots the tracker, the FM1’s keys enter steps, and a browser page manages its cartridge, songs, and ROM. Its README says installation and playback have been confirmed on hardware. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: FM1 Tonic
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine inspired by Sonic Charge’s Microtonic, with an engine of its own and no connection with Sonic Charge: eight synthesised drum voices, a sequencer with accents, fills, and up to 64 steps, 16 patterns a preset chained into songs, an eight-track mixer, reverb, delay, and a master compressor. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE’s firmware back, or from its release package, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FM1-Hero
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A falling-note piano trainer and rhythm game built with foma: bars for each hand fall down the screen while the key lights show the next notes, with a mode that waits for the right key, a scored game mode, a loop between two points, and 16 built-in songs and a slot for a MIDI file of your own, all played on a six-voice FM synth. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: FM1_AudioBase
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The FM1 as a USB audio interface and nothing more: what the computer plays reaches the FM1's outputs, MASTER sets the volume, and GLO shows a visualiser, and it is meant as a small base to start new firmware from. Its README says both USB audio streams, MASTER, and the visualiser were tested on an FM1, and calls it very early development. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: FM1 YOGA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Sounds for the final relaxation of a yoga class: guided programs on a held tone at 174, 396, 432 or 528 Hz with a slow pulsing rhythm, breathing noise, singing bowls and a generative ambient garden from AMB-1, with a handpan, kalimba, tongue drum, bowls or chimes to play on the keys. Its screen speaks German, English or Sanskrit, and its site is in German. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FM1-800
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fan-made Korg Poly-800 built on Felucca: its 64 factory programs and 64 slots of your own, its chorus, and its 256-note step sequencer, with a phaser, a tape echo, and MIDI clock in. Its README says it is not made or endorsed by Korg or M-VAVE. Its one release, a pre-release, carries the package.

firmwares.title: fm1-amy
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: AMY's emulations of the Roland Juno-60's 128 factory patches as a six-voice synth, built on X0X, shaped with the AMYboard editor's patch knobs on eleven pages, and editable live from that editor over USB. Its README says it has been built, installed and played on one FM1. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page with the project's Python tool.

firmwares.title: fm1-radio
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An internet radio over WiFi: it joins a 2.4 GHz network, plays stations from Radio Garden's map, and puts punch-in effects on the keys. Its first release, 1.0, was withdrawn after crashing on some FM1s when WiFi started; 1.3.1 is a pre-release, whose notes ask anyone whose FM1 crashes to report it. It installs from its own browser page, with a manual on the same site.

firmwares.title: fm1-wheel
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A tonewheel organ after setBfree, with drawbars, percussion, a Leslie with slow, fast and stop rotor, drive and reverb, on fm1-base and felucca-bsp. Its README says the FM1 build has been flashed and tested on a real FM1 (8 Nov), and that its SMK-37 Pro build passes its host tests but has not been flashed yet. It installs from its own page, which carries both builds.

firmwares.title: FM1-RDX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-operator FM synth inspired by Yamaha’s reface DX, with 32 sounds in four banks, up to seven voices, editing of each operator and envelope, and two effects. It records over USB and exchanges voices with Yamaha’s Soundmondo as a reface DX. Since 1.0.1 it stores named voices in 32 user slots, and records phrases in a looper with four draft slots. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: FM1-SF2
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A 40-voice, sixteen-channel General MIDI sound module that plays a bank made from a SoundFont (.sf2), converted in the browser and installed separately. Parts can be soloed or muted while a song plays, and more than one sound can be layered on a channel. It installs from its own browser page, which also sends banks, and can be tried in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FM1-TRAX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A Mega Drive music tracker with VGM export, and a desktop editor on the same engine. Its README says it has been tested on a real FM1, and its site plays it in a browser and installs the latest release.

firmwares.title: FMav-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A semi-modular mono synth built on OberVave 3.3.2: a VCO, a self-oscillating four-pole ladder filter, an LFO, an ADSR, a VCA, a wave folder, sample and hold, a mixer, and a patchbay with normals and dummy plugs, with four tracks, MIDI clock sync, chorus, delay, reverb, and 90 sounds. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: FMEL-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Mellotron-style firmware built on Dinghy, playing tapes recorded from a 1973 Mellotron M400S: it mixes two of them and colours them with effects and lo-fi tape effects. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FMER
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Six-operator FM and Virtual Analog synthesis with four-track sequencing and songs. FMER Companion, a Windows app, installs it and keeps instruments, projects, and backups on the computer, with DX7 import and export. Build 736 adds Bluetooth MIDI between two FM-1 units.

firmwares.title: FM Lab
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A six-operator FM synthesizer made for learning FM: no drums or song mode, just the DX7 engine with every parameter under a knob while the sound plays, and a screen that shows what you changed.
