It has eight voices, 32 user slots, a small arpeggiator and a one-phrase looper, and is built on Dinghy. Its README says it runs on the FM1, and it installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Doom
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: Doom on the FM1, by sloopDX's author: one arena from the free FreeDM, played on the keys and knob with the FM1's screen as the display and synthesised sound effects, but no music. It installs from its own browser page, which can put sloopDX back, and keeps sloopDX's USB rescue. It needs no game data of your own.

firmwares.title: FM-1 firmware patcher
firmwares.status: Works with this editor Patches V15 and V16 Updated 28 Oct 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A script that changes your own copy of M-VAVE's V15 or V16 rather than a firmware of its own: operator detune matches Dexed, aftertouch no longer brings a strong vibrato, and the main screen's scope turns dark blue. The FM1 still reports V15 or V16, so this editor treats it as M-VAVE's firmware. The patched file may not be shared, so you run the Python script yourself. M-UPGRADE sees it as the V15 already installed, so go down to V14 with M-VAVE's tone updater first, then install it; the same steps put V15 back.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Macropad Patch
firmwares.status: Works with this editor Patches V15 · Latest 1.1.0 Updated 22 Nov 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A patcher, not a firmware, which changes your own copy of M-VAVE’s V15 so that every button, key, and knob sends a USB-MIDI note, fourteen buttons, 27 keys, and seven knobs each way, which an app such as Keyboard Maestro or MidiKey2Key turns into shortcuts. The synth functions go, and so does the settings screen, so set the velocity you want with M-VAVE’s firmware before patching. Since 1.1.0 its release also carries the patched firmware, ready to install with M-UPGRADE. The patched file may not be shared, so you download V15 yourself and patch it in the web page or with Python, then install it with M-UPGRADE. Its README says no recovery method is known if an update fails; M-VAVE’s updater puts V15 back.

firmwares.title: FM-1 MIDI Processor
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock). Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A stand-alone MIDI processor, with no computer needed. The synth is removed, so the only sound is a metronome click. MIDI from TRS and USB goes through a pipeline and comes out of USB, with a searchable monitor showing what it did to each message, per-port channel and message filters, and message and channel remaps. Event triggers send a list of messages, such as the bank and program changes for a whole rig, from one incoming message. The knobs send CCs, the keys play notes and send program and bank changes, and clock lockout keeps clocks from being merged. It holds 16 named patches, which can be dumped and loaded over SysEx, and it is built on the Official Open V14 source. Latency measured on an FM-1 averages under 0.2 ms. It installs from its own page in desktop Chrome or Edge over USB.

firmwares.title: FM-1 NES
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: Plays NES games on the FM1: its 27 keys are the controller and its screen the television. It is the worked example in a kit for writing FM1 firmware from scratch, published as source with no installer page or ready-made release, and no game included. It makes no music.

firmwares.title: FM-106
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock).
firmwares.blurb: A six-voice Juno-106 emulation, ported from ultramaster_kr106: PolyBLEP oscillators with a sub-oscillator and noise, a 24 dB resonant ladder filter, a four-position high-pass, the 106’s envelope, a BBD stereo chorus, and 128 factory patches decoded from a Juno-106’s SysEx, under Roland-styled screens. It renders voices on both cores, as Melodee does. Its release carries a package to install.

firmwares.title: FM1 Quest
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP as a pixel-art RPG. The four tracks are four heroes, every lit step is an attack, the tempo sets how fast the party walks, the key picks the biome, effects bring the weather, and recording a loop is a boss fight against the King Slime. Every SLOOP function stays where it was, with the same controls. Its page installs it from Chrome or Edge, and the installer can put M-VAVE's firmware back.

firmwares.title: fm1-chord
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord machine built on Felucca: the white keys at the left play the scale's chords and those to their right strum them, as on an Omnichord, while the black keys add sevenths, ninths, suspensions, and borrowed chords. It adds a chord sequencer, drum loops, a looper, and an ear trainer. It runs on an FM1 but installs from a terminal, with a script from its source.

firmwares.title: FM1 Cofrade
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Holy Week firmware built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open V14 SDK, which replaces the sixteen factory projects with original marches for cornets, trumpets, and drums in the style of Semana Santa bands. Its README, in Spanish, says it has been installed and checked on an FM1, though its sounds have not yet been listened to there. Its page plays it in a simulator and installs it over M-VAVE's V15 or Official Open.

firmwares.title: fm1-d50
firmwares.status: Work in progress · Latest 0.95 Updated 25 Nov 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock).
firmwares.blurb: A Roland D-50 on fm1-base, using PicoFaceD5’s engine: 16 voices, every key mode, the D-50’s reverb, chorus, and EQ, its SysEx for editors and librarians, and its display. No Roland data is included: you make a data file from your own D-50’s ROM and bank dumps, and its browser page installs the firmware and writes your data. Its README calls it a work in progress. It plays in a browser with the same data file.

firmwares.title: fm1-dock
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: One firmware, installed once, that holds several synths as modules in flash: hold HOME to pick another, with no reinstall. It comes with CS-1, Scintilla, OberVave, FM-1 SID, and a sine, and its page deploys your own modules over USB and shows the log and the load. Version 0.9 adds Animatek's ATEK303 and KEYS, a clavinet, an electric piano, and a piano from physical models. It installs from its release package or the Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: FM1-GM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A General MIDI sound module and sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments, and a drum kit on track 10. It stores up to 64 songs of up to 128 measures each. Its README says the author tested it on a real FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a web editor.

firmwares.title: FM1 Keyboard Academy
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A first keyboard course: eight chapters from finding middle C, twelve exercises, and thirty traditional melodies, each played to you, lit on the keys, and listened to, with the FM synthesiser and its DX7 presets still behind the learning screen. Its README says the preview has been installed on an FM1 and the whole course still needs playing through. It installs from its pre-release package.

firmwares.title: FM-1 Neverhood
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: 22 presets, a four-track sequencer, and a battery indicator, built on fm1-base around The Neverhood: its build takes the game's sprites and sounds from the demo ScummVM offers and samples from Terry Scott Taylor's recordings. Its page plays it in a browser emulator and installs it.

firmwares.title: FMDj
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: LSDj, the Game Boy tracker, and DMGo!, the drum machine, run in a Game Boy emulator inside the FM1's firmware, on its screen, keys, knobs, and sound, by Hortator's maker. You bring your own ROM: the install page puts it into the firmware in your browser and installs one of the two at a time, and a simulator tries it first.

firmwares.title: FMini-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Minimoog Model D emulation, built on Felucca, with onboard effects, an arpeggiator, and a sequencer. Its page installs the firmware over USB from a browser, and an emulator there plays it first. Since 2.5.12 it also builds for the SMK-37.

firmwares.title: FMtribe
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware after the Korg monotribe: one oscillator, a two-pole filter, an LFO, three drums and an eight-step sequencer, written without Korg code. So far it is an early test build that plays fm1-base’s test voice under its name; the instrument itself comes next. It installs from its own browser page, which also has an emulator, a quickstart and a manual.

firmwares.title: FMLarynx
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A formant synthesiser with a 303-style 16-step pattern sequencer, ported from a VST3 plugin and built on Dinghy. A saw wave runs through a three-formant vowel filter, a resonant low-pass and a ping-pong delay, with vowel, accent and slide per step and 16 stored patterns. It installs from its release package, or through the FM-1 Firmware Hub; the README says the sound engine, controls and sequencer were tested on the FM-1.

firmwares.title: FMY262
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: An 18-channel OPL3 tracker in the spirit of Adlib Tracker II: patterns, instruments of two or four operators, percussion mode, and Adlib Tracker II’s effects and macros, on the FM1’s screen, knobs, and keys. Its workbench page installs it, moves songs between the FM1 and a computer over USB, imports Adlib Tracker II and Reality AdLib Tracker songs, and runs the firmware in a browser.

firmwares.title: FN ACID
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware where every track is a function drawn on one pair of axes and played as it is drawn. Its ACID track plays sixteen steps you write, the 303's way, or a formula, through a ping-pong delay and a small room, with punch-in effects. It is built on Dinghy, SLOOP, and Felucca, comes as numbered test builds, and installs from its own web page.

firmwares.title: FNTSMG-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox on Felucca: eight tracks, four of drums and four of synths, 26 engines with SAMPLE on every track, 32 steps a track with conditions and probability, and eight-track USB audio. Its screen reads in Spanish, English, or Portuguese. It installs free from its own browser page, which invites an optional contribution, or from its release package, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: FOMAJAM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing.
firmwares.blurb: A nine-track groovebox in which each track plays its own machine: modelled and sampled classic drum machines, your own samples, Felucca’s synth engines, or MIDI out. It has eight 16-step patterns with accents, slides, and ratchets, and sends and distortion. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: FoMni
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord harp inspired by the Suzuki Omnichord: the 16 white keys are the strum plate and the 11 black keys pick the chord, with rhythm patterns, an auto bass, and its own effects. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back.

firmwares.title: FORMALFRED
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative sequencer of four lanes whose sequencing logic is proved in Lean 4, made at a hackathon. Its site has a web installer and a browser simulator, its licence is GPL-3.0, and its README does not say it has been heard on an FM1.

firmwares.title: FRASIL
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An instrument for ambient drones and textures: you latch drones and chords in a key, play icy FM bells over them by hand, through an arpeggiator, or from a 32-step sequencer, and since 2.0 a bass line of its own, all into a large reverb with shimmer and freeze. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package, and its notes are in English and French.

firmwares.title: FREITAKT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Hortator fork with an Elektron Model:Cycles workflow: six tracks with Hortator’s machines and a chord machine, free polymeter with a master length of up to 1,024 steps, parameter and machine locks, and arpeggios and retrigs on every track and step, with the sequencer sent out over MIDI. It cannot read Hortator’s projects. It installs from its release package; the installer page and manual its README describes are not yet attached to the release.

firmwares.title: Frodhes
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Physically modelled Fender Rhodes, vibraphone, and marimba with no samples, plus effects, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales, and presets. It comes as a release package, and a browser emulator plays it first.

firmwares.title: Frodhes-Bark
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Frodhes with physically modelled Rhodes and Wurlitzer electric pianos, a vibraphone, and a marimba, with no samples. It adds a six-point velocity curve and stereo effects, and it also has builds for the SMK-37.

firmwares.title: FuMi-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A shigin accompaniment instrument grown from FoMni, inspired by Suikohsha's ST-50: the white keys are its lower row and the black keys its upper row or koto ornaments, in equal temperament or the ST-50's own just tuning, with koto, sho, shakuhachi, flute, and taiko voices on a six-operator FM engine. Its own page installs it and plays it in a browser first.

firmwares.title: FX-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: AISLING FX-1, a fork of AISLING that puts sound from a computer, over USB, through AISLING’s effects. Its README says 1.0 has run on one FM1 with a Mac playing through it, and that its saves share the FM1’s memory with AISLING’s. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: GabberBuddy
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware based on Felucca and XOX. It installs from its web installer, in Chrome or Edge, which also has a Back to the stock firmware button.

firmwares.title: GABBERKIX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A hardcore kick designer by Presethead: each kick is built from a midbody, a punch, and a sub driven hard into clippers, with a randomiser, sixteen presets, resampling, and MIDI clock. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE’s firmware back, and a second page renders its presets to audio files.

firmwares.title: GameDude
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A Game Boy emulator by Doom FM-1 / SMK’s maker. Its browser page installs it on an FM1 or an SMK-37, plays Game Boy cartridges in a simulator, and sends them to a game library on the device over USB or Bluetooth.

firmwares.title: GammaWave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A synth firmware based on Felucca, with a wavetable sound, a live spectrogram filter, a four-track tape deck, and a song generator with 49 genres. It has a web studio and installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: GATOR
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A macro-oscillator firmware inspired by Mutable Instruments' Plaits. It installs from its own web installer.

firmwares.title: GHOULBOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca fork for dungeon synth, dark ambient, and fantasy music: a cathedral-sized HALL reverb, a worn-cassette TAPE effect, a hurdy-gurdy engine with tunable drones and a buzzing trompette, and 59 sounds, from crypt pads and monk choirs to a sampled bowed psaltery, chamber organ, and folk harp, all behind an old-RPG screen with a skull at boot. It installs from its own browser page, which saves a full backup first.

firmwares.title: GIO-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative disco machine in the style of Giorgio Moroder: it plays itself from power-on with bass, strings, a lead and drums, across nine song presets you steer by key, pattern and section. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser emulator first. Its 0.3.1-beta notes call it beta, installed on three FM1s so far with no major issues reported, and still advise installing with caution.

firmwares.title: GL!TCH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A neon-noir groovebox built on GR!MM, by Coqui’s maker: four tracks, seven sources, tape and megacity space effects, scales including Insen, Hirajoshi, and Iwato, and 44 factory sounds after Blade Runner, on a glitched landscape that tears with the sound. Its README says 2.0 was tested on a real FM1, and 2.0.2 not yet. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: GLIDER
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone synthesiser built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open: white keys latch scale tones, black keys glide them, with a tape echo, ladder filter, shimmer reverb and a quiet microsound drum track. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser simulator is available. The README says it has run on one FM1 and no licence is stated on GitHub.

firmwares.title: GLITCH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine for fine glitch and microsound beats, built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open: every sound is synthesised (clicks, click trains, digital crunch, noise snaps, micro kicks), loops can mutate from bar to bar, and stutter, ratchet and reverse effects sit on the keys. Its README says it ran on one FM-1 in October 2026, with a CPU load below 30%, and no licence is stated. It installs from its own browser page, and a simulator is available.

firmwares.title: Gnomad
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Easy, kid-friendly firmware built on Felucca, with sound pictures instead of menus, four colour knobs, and a singing gnome. It comes as a release package, installed with a Python script.

firmwares.title: Golana
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: One analogue-style synth laid out like the microKORG, a Felucca fork with two oscillators, five filters, two envelopes, two LFOs, a patch bay, an arpeggiator, and a step sequencer, every page drawing what it does. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Golana DZ Edition
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Golana that adds a 64-step sequencer, a song mode, and USB MIDI out. Its README says these were tested on a physical FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Golf
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A wavetable synthesiser with a 32-step sequencer, its engine written for the FM1 rather than ported from the Golf plug-in, whose wavetables and 96 of whose presets it uses: two morphing oscillators with unison and warp, sub and noise, a filter with five types, two envelopes and two LFOs, and drive, OTT compression, chorus, delay, and reverb, with 168 presets. It installs from its own browser page, which can put the stock firmware back.

firmwares.title: GR!MM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Dark ambient, dungeon synth, and deathdream firmware: four drone and atmosphere tracks with seven sound sources, long dark effects, and a 64-step sequencer per track. It installs from the Firmware Hub, or by hand from its release file, and has a browser version and an editor.

firmwares.title: GRAIN PIANO
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A sampled grand piano that a granulator breaks into grains, built on fm1-base and inspired by Tonitor: each note plays the Salamander Grand Piano and sends grains out of the same sample, with eight presets of two macros each, a hold, and backwards grains. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, plays in a browser, and has manuals in English and German.

firmwares.title: GRIDLIGHT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A 16 × 16 light-grid sequencer instrument after Yamaha's Tenori-On, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma, with a song of 16 blocks saved to flash. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Groove OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track groovebox that keeps an FM synth and adds a virtual analogue synth and drum kits, with a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, a six-effect mixer, and a performance mode with scenes. Version 2.0 adds a sampler that records from a phone over Bluetooth or USB, or from the FM1 itself, Bluetooth audio, and a wider stereo mix; 1.4 owners update to it free. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's V15 back, and has a browser emulator to try first.

firmwares.title: Guitchordi
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-string guitar strummer for the FM1, with 16 instruments, chord parts, strum patterns and fourteen tunings. It installs from its beta release package (.fwsc). The README reports it installed and played on one FM1, while recovery restoration after an interrupted write is untested. A browser simulator is available.

firmwares.title: Guru-600
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock). Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A Prophet-600 emulator built on Felucca: two oscillators per voice with sync, a 24 dB filter with its own envelope, Poly-Mod, two LFOs and six or eight voices, with 255 sounds including the P600's 100 factory programs, MORPH and MUTATE, and P600 .syx transfer. Felucca's four tracks, sequencer and other engines stay. It installs from its own page in Chrome or Edge, with a browser editor and a user guide in seven languages.

firmwares.title: GWAAN-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient drone, built on fm1-base, that plays itself from power-on: gliding FM voices, a swelling sub drone and pad, wind and water noise, and distant radio-like pings, in five scenes steered with knob macros. Its notes are in Japanese with an English summary. It installs from its release package with a browser installer.

firmwares.title: h1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Fourteen instruments, each a full-screen animated picture you play, from lo-fi keys and analogue pads to chiptune, plucked strings, and a drum kit, with eight algorithms and four live knobs, a loop recorder, a step sequencer, an arpeggiator, and a metronome. Its README says its releases have been installed and played on one FM1. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package, and plays in a browser simulator.

firmwares.title: HADAL-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generative dark ambient, by DARK-1's maker: drones, choirs, bells, and 135 sound effects that change by themselves across 15 worlds, with 40 melting pictures, while the keys play bells or latch choir voices. Its README says it works on FM1s with either flash chip. It installs from its release package with an FM1 web installer, and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Haunted FM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Five generative firmwares for haunted ambient music with meaningful controls: Halflight, Midnight, Untrue, Voicemail, and Worntape. Its flasher page installs any of them from Chrome or Edge, and the release carries a package for each.

firmwares.title: HAWK CHUA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chaotic synthesiser whose oscillator is Chua's circuit, with each voice a circuit solver and the screen drawing its attractor live. It adds Rings-style resonators and waveguides and a shimmer reverb, on a cut-down Felucca base. It installs from its release package (.fwsc) or the installer page that GitHub builds. The README is in Dutch.

firmwares.title: HERA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A chord groovebox after Roland's AIRA Compact J-6, built on Dinghy: 100 chord sets, nine phrase styles of 12 variations each, and a 64-pattern step sequencer. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put the factory firmware back, and its Workbench plays it in a browser.

firmwares.title: Hookology
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Melodee 1.6.1 fork for catching an idea fast, as a chord, a strum, a loop, or a hook, with HERA’s chord sets and features after SLOOP. It installs from its own browser page, which backs the FM1 up first and can put M-VAVE’s V15 back.

firmwares.title: Hortator
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine built on Felucca: eight drum tracks of 808, 909, and Plaits drum models and samples, a 64-step sequencer with motion recording and songs, Mutable Instruments' Grids, a compressor for ducking and pumping, resonators, and live performance effects. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser first, and leaves through M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE.

firmwares.title: Hungry Travis
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A spoon-feeding balance game: keep the bean in the bowl, approach an increasingly grumpy face, and tip the spoon to deliver the bite. Its FM-1_797 release carries the package, its source, and a quick-start guide, and its notes say it was verified on an FM1 with the original flash chip. It installs with the USB MIDI installer in its source archive.

firmwares.title: HYP-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A generative techno machine built on AMB-1, with MIDI out per voice. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back. The same page offers four more experimental RedtailWorks firmwares: LOF-1, ECO-1, and GRAV-1, which its README says have not yet run on an FM1, and, since 22 October, CTY-1, in which a growing city plays the FM1. Since 6 November the repository also has BIT-1, a generative 8-bit tracker with an install page of its own, which its README says has run only in the simulator and the browser emulator.

firmwares.title: HYPNOTIC MIKE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track arranger for hypnotic, looping techno, built on Official Open: each layer, from the drone and kick to the hats and percussion, has presets of its own, and sixteen factory sets load all eight at once. It draws in two shades of green, like an old phone screen. Its README says it was tested on an FM1, and it installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE’s V15 back.

firmwares.title: Impressionism
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient firmware in which voices drift on their own slow timers inside Impressionist harmony: whole-tone and pentatonic scales, extended and quartal chords, and planing over a pedal tone. It is built to drift rather than be played. It installs from its release package, and can be tried in a browser emulator first. Its README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.

firmwares.title: IND-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A self-playing industrial machine after the records of KMFDM, Nine Inch Nails, and Ministry: it starts as soon as it is switched on and arranges its own songs, with song and drum editors. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: InfeKt-FM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A virtual analogue polysynth modelled on the Access Virus, which its README says is compatible with Virus patches: three oscillators a voice with a sub oscillator, noise, and a ring modulator. Its README says it runs on both FM1 hardware versions. It installs from its own browser page, which has a guide.

firmwares.title: INSERT COIN
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The chiptune sibling of CHORD RUN: one-finger chords in the style of video game tunes on the black keys and a melody on the white keys, with 17 chip sounds, Game Boy-style drums, and a drum studio for grooves of your own, while an early-80s arcade shooter plays along, its ship firing on every key. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: J6
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-voice polysynth after the Roland JUNO-60, built on fm1-base: band-limited saw and pulse oscillators with a sub and noise, a 24 dB resonant filter, one shared envelope, an arpeggiator, and a status page with a pattern strip. It installs from its release package with the Firmware Hub installer.

firmwares.title: Jam Playground
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative groovebox: it starts playing on power-up, and each boot makes a new song that you can mutate, change scale and tempo of, and jam along with. It has sampled instruments, drums, a recorded keyboard loop and four live effect knobs. It installs from its release package (.fwsc) over USB, with a command-line installer in the repo; the README says installing is at your own risk and gives steps to restore M-VAVE's firmware.

firmwares.title: JamesOS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox built on Dinghy and Felucca, with three synth tracks on 24 Plaits engines, 128 starting sounds, and a four-lane drum kit. It has a pattern sequencer with an arranger, effects on each track with a shared reverb, LFOs, and twelve named project slots that its browser editor imports and exports. firmwares.blurb: A singing songwriter. A pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, consonants and all, over FM chords, bass and drums, in a voice synthesised live rather than sampled. You shape her voice with five characters, effects, harmony, whisper and fry, write patterns or let GEN write a whole song, and watch her dance. From 0.7 the chords and bass play on a six-operator DX7 engine, and it takes MIDI input. It installs from its own page in Chrome or Edge and has a browser emulator. The code is GPL-3.0-only; the singer is Hatsune Miku fan art under Crypton's Piapro Character License, free and non-commercial use only.

firmwares.title: MIN-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A small minimalist ensemble that plays itself from the moment it starts, in the manner of Philip Glass: repeating figures, slow chord cycles, and processes you can hear, in four models. You take over as much as you like, playing chords, bringing parts in and out, and recording songs. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Mini-Tone
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Stephane Schmitz's firmware based on Felucca 1.5, with six tracks instead of four and new engines, five of them based on Elektron machines, plus Braids, a TB-303, and SID. It adds a ping-pong delay and a reverb of its own, and installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Mini-Vision
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A wavetable synthesiser after Roland's n/vision, forked from Mini-Tone. Two wavetable layers with 63 tables, a sine-fold wave shaper, phase modulation, and a choice of filters, with the interface drawn after the n/vision's. It keeps Mini-Tone's TR-808 engine and installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: MNM-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track synth forked from Hortator 0.23.3: six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a resonant filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, and parameter locks and slides. Its README says it has been tested on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays the real firmware in a browser.

firmwares.title: Mocky
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A developer tool, not an instrument: it shows pictures sent from a web page on the FM1's screen, to check screen mockups on the real hardware, and can keep up to 64 in flash. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: MODELAR
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators sound all the time and modulate each other, while the keys move a cursor on an XY pad, with gestures, a sequencer, and eight generative environments. It installs from The Firmware Hub or its release package.

firmwares.title: Modular-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A modular synth after the Nord Modular: its web app builds patches from modules, maps their parameters and the knobs through a matrix, and uploads them to the FM1, which steps through patches and modules and adds an arpeggiator with Euclidean rhythms and chaos. Version 1.0.3 plays four voices. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Modular One
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Film-music firmware built on Felucca. Its README says it runs on the author's FM1 and has not been tested on other units. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: MONO2K
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Monomachine-style firmware of six tracks, each one machine, with a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, and a lofi bus. Its README says it runs on an FM1, and it installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Monohull
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A monosynth of one voice, with the whole CPU spent on it: analogue-modelled oscillators, five filters (transistor ladder, diode ladder, OTA cascade, Sallen-Key, and state-variable), unison, a Juno-style chorus, delay, reverb, and 14 factory presets. It shows up over USB as a MIDI device and keeps nothing in flash, so other firmwares' projects and samples are left alone. Its README says it has been tested on a real FM1.

firmwares.title: Moondaw
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A tracker with eight tracks, instruments you build yourself, three effects a step, and songs kept as plain text files that an LLM can write. Its README calls it a beta tried on a real FM1 every day, and it installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: MOPE-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A sad wavetable synth forked from FiMba-1: eight tables and six voices, a toy-keyboard backing band of 13 gloomy beats with an auto-bass, and a pixel creature in a rainy alley whose face shows the sound. Its README calls it a beta tested on a real FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it.

firmwares.title: MORPHEUS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track groovebox after Propellerhead's ReBirth, with an 808, a 909, two 303s, Amen breaks, an FM lead, a sub synth, and a MIDI track, sequenced in the style of Reason's Matrix. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator and a manual.

firmwares.title: MOSS-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient firmware on fm1-base: lo-fi, nature scenes, and slow generative loops, with a looper that listens to what you play. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Mutable Dreams
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Kid Bunka's six-track instrument built on Mutable Instruments' open engines: start from one of 272 factory Biomes, let its patterns evolve, then link up to eight sections in the Journey Arranger and record the moments to keep, with a six-track sequencer grid, 632 tone presets, and USB audio with each voice on its own input. Its notes say 2.0 was tested on an FM1. It has a browser instrument and hardware editor, an illustrated walkthrough, and installs from its browser installer or release package.

firmwares.title: Mycelium
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Forest, Psytrance, Goa, and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP, with its own drum assets and icons. Its release is a test package, with an installation guide on the maker's site.

firmwares.title: NAIWAN 91
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: City pop and coastal firmware: nineteen genres, ten urban and nine coastal, that play themselves while you steer, each with ten jam pieces on the firmware’s own FM, analogue and percussion engines. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator.

firmwares.title: NACHTFAHRT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative Berlin School instrument after Tangerine Dream, Klaus Schulze and Ashra: long, repeating sequences and slowly evolving textures that play themselves, with the white keys giving a melody in the piece's key and the firmware answering what you play. It was called BERLIN while it was built. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Nano Freak
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Freak-style paraphonic synth built on FMini-1: fifteen oscillator types, a state-variable or ladder filter, a cycling envelope, two LFOs, a modulation matrix, an arpeggiator and a 64-step sequencer, and 58 factory presets. Its README says 3.0.0 was tested on a real FM1, and that its SMK-37 builds are beta. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: NCC
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Novation Circuit Companion, a Felucca fork that turns the FM1 into a two-part synth for the Novation Circuit Tracks: part L plays the Circuit’s MIDI 1 track and part R its MIDI 2, with twelve engines and 161 sounds picked by role, and the Circuit’s eight macro knobs mapped to each engine’s parameters. It has no sequencer of its own: the Circuit plays the notes and sends the clock. It installs from its own browser page, which can return the FM1 to V15.

firmwares.title: Nauclerus
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox based on Hortator, with eight tracks of drums, up to two acid bass voices, 64-step patterns, a remix mode, a TB-3PO generator, Grids, motion, parameter locks, and per-track LFOs. It installs from its own browser page, which also runs it in a simulator.

firmwares.title: NEON
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A synthwave groovebox forked from Felucca: Juno-style pads, supersaw leads, basses, and 80s drum machines, about 220 presets sorted by role, and a sequencer that follows one chord progression across every track. Its README says it was tested on a real FM1 and calls it a young project. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Niagara Drift
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone synth with two always-on drones you tune, shape, and move rather than play note by note, inspired by the Stylophone CPM DS-2, the Moog Subharmonicon, and the Soma Lyra-8. Version 0.3 redraws every page and adds sixteen presets, eight gestures, and eleven tunings; 0.3.1 runs heavy sounds more smoothly. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it without an FM1.

firmwares.title: NIGHTFALL
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A cyberpunk-inspired performance synth with a sequencer, effects, and a browser studio. Its README says the package has booted on one FM1 and passed its protocol tests there. It installs from its own browser updater.

firmwares.title: NJA TACK
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca-derived firmware of moving harmony and played MIDI. Its README calls 6.28-rc5 an experimental review candidate, installed once on an FM1 on 10 Nov, with its listening, timing, and recovery tests still open. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: NOCT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A permanent MIDI preset for the FM1 with FL Studio and Ableton Live scripts, drawn as an animated night city with six scenes for chords, composing, rhythm, arpeggios, and sync. Its README, in Russian, is on version 0.9.4, and it installs from its own page with a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: No Man Sky FM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A space adventure based on SLOOP 2.7.1: one hand flies the ship with two knobs while the other plays the music. Land on planets, mine, fight robots, and warp between stars. It installs from its own browser page, which also runs the firmware in a 3D simulator with sound.

firmwares.title: MONK-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Twelve singers from MonkSynth, a formant vocal synthesiser after the Delay Lama plug-in, each with its own character and a mouth that follows the vowel. It reads velocity and aftertouch from the FM1's own keys, with no hardware changes, so pressing harder moves the vowel or bends the pitch. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried first in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: NOIZ DEMONS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca mod in which every randomised sound is answered by one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, whose sigil takes over the screen. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Norilsk
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware for inhospitable soundscapes: three generators drawn at random, three effect slots to wreck them, and a master delay and plate reverb. Its README calls it for ambient hellscapes and barren atmospheres, and it installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: NU//METAL SKRATCHMASTER PRO
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A robot turntablist with a nu metal band: the speech synthesiser SAM says 27 words onto a virtual record that you scratch with the keys and jog wheel, over drop-tuned guitars, a bass, and a 12-piece kit locked to ten grooves. Its README says it runs on the FM1, and it installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: OberVave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-voice analogue-style polysynth in the spirit of the American poly synths of 1979–84: two oscillators a voice with hard sync and cross-modulation, a 12 or 24 dB filter that morphs from lowpass to highpass, two envelopes, an LFO, an arpeggiator, a two-track step sequencer, 99 programs, and chorus, delay, and plate reverb. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub. Its README warns against 1.1, whose USB-MIDI out is broken and which no installer can replace once it runs; 1.2 fixed it.

firmwares.title: OBSCURA LINE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A train adventure built on Dinghy: drive a train round a synthwave loop line, mend forgotten machines through mechanical puzzles, synth jams, and rhythm games, and uncover the mystery at its heart. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package, and has a guide.

firmwares.title: ObsSynth
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-voice synth built on Hortator, after the ObsSynth desktop instruments: two oscillators with standard, supersaw, wavetable, and granular engines, a sub, noise, sync and ring modulation, a multimode filter, two envelopes, two LFOs, and poly, mono, legato, and unison modes. Its README says 0.1.0 was tested on an FM1. It installs from its release package, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: OCA-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: An ocarina for the FM1, for games that listen, such as Ocarina of Time on a Switch 2. It installs from the signed release package, and its website has the manual.

firmwares.title: OCTODRONE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-voice drone synth after the SOMA Laboratory Lyra-8, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma, with eight panels saved to flash. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: OFFWORLD
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone synth in the spirit of 1980s science-fiction film scores, on fm1-base: two detuned saws and a sine sub for each voice, a 24 dB filter with a brass envelope, an ensemble chorus, a ping-pong delay, and a reverb that rings for up to 30 seconds or freezes. Every knob is a macro that rests on named sweet spots. It installs from its release package, plays in a browser, and has manuals in English and German.

firmwares.title: OG Synth
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A synth firmware by Mike Johnson Beats with 16 engines, 28 effects, and four tracks that play at once. It installs from the browser installer on its site, which links a backup of your presets first, and the site carries a manual and a version history. Only the application part of its source is published, under MPL-2.0; its sound engines, effects, and sequencer are proprietary.

firmwares.title: Ombak
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A gamelan-inspired instrument by Lunar Eclipse Forge, mostly Balinese and made for meditative atmospheres: you play the core melody on the white keys and the ensemble weaves interlocking parts and gongs around it, in Balinese and Javanese tunings. It runs on Penumbra's platform, installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: OP dream
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An OP-1-style way of working built on Skiff 2.6: a tape on the home screen keeps what you play as you played it, with no quantising, on six tracks recorded one after the other or on top of each other, beside a step sequencer. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: OpenIFW
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A port of OpenIFW’s monophonic synthesiser, with four oscillators, two main filters, two LFOs, and a full effects chain. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a demo, and its notes are in Chinese.

firmwares.title: OpenVALive
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Formerly OpenLiveSynth, a live-first instrument: a virtual analogue synth and a drum machine on four tracks with loops of their own, CAPTURE to turn what you just played into the loop, scenes with a knob that morphs between them, hold-to-play effects, and a Creative Engine that mutates, fills, or simplifies loops. Its numbering started again at 0.0.1 in a new repository on 19 Nov. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in an emulator.

firmwares.title: OPLBend Tracker
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: An LSDJ-style tracker on an OPL3-style FM engine, with 18 voices, effects inspired by circuit bending, a drum machine and a looper. It opens and exports AdLib Tracker II songs, and also runs on a Mac as a VST3 plugin. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: OPLBOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: The FM1 as an AdLib: an OPL2 emulation that plays SoundFX Macs Opera songs, the DOS soundtracks of LINEL’s games and Stone Age, and since 0.4 a tracker that edits and saves them as .CMF files. Its README says earlier versions ran on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: OPN-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: The Mega Drive's sound chips as a synth: recreations of the YM2612 and the SN76489, with a library of 128 FM patches. Its web app fills the library from .opm files or a game's VGM music, edits the patches, and streams the original songs to the FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: OPX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Felucca 1.5.1 with one more engine, an altered-FM engine after the Korg opsix: six operators routed by an algorithm, EGs, LFOs, a filter, and effects. Everything Felucca does stays. A project with an OPX track opens only on OPX. It has a browser simulator and an editor with an OPX tab, and installs from its own page, which can return the FM1 to M-VAVE’s V15.

firmwares.title: OPX Solo
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The OPX firmware with the OPX engine alone: one part, with the memory of all four parts, so every opsix effect type fits and the short delay reaches 300 ms. Other tracks of a project stay in it but are silent. It has its own browser simulator and editor, and installs from its own page.

firmwares.title: Optimist
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A modular firmware built on SLOOP, Felucca, Melodee, X0X, and other FM1 projects: you choose its engines, drum kits, effects, and features in a browser builder with a live flash and RAM budget, try the build in a simulator, and install it from the same site. Its releases come in ready-made flavours; 0.3 added Ableton Link and SD card support, and its new memory layout erased projects saved in flash, so back them up in the web editor before updating from an earlier release. Its README calls it early access and says it runs on real FM1s while most features are tested in the emulator and on a computer.

firmwares.title: ORBIT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox built on SLOOP with screens inspired by the OP-1: synth, drum, mixer, and an event tape for copying and moving what the four tracks play, with engines of its own beside SLOOP's and a six-operator FM. Its releases carry only the firmware file, installed from a terminal with a script from its source rather than a browser page, and it plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: ORBITA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative instrument whose three FM voices play interlocking rhythms while the screen draws their orbits, in four scenes with density, phase, and FM ratio on the knobs, and the same notes and voices as its browser and plug-in versions. Its FM1 firmware is a beta, installed from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: OrGigs
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An organ built on Dinghy: three manuals with 84 free-running tone generators and no voice stealing, eight models from tonewheel and combo organs to pipe organs and free reeds, drawbars, percussion, rotary, drive, delay, and reverb, 16 performance setups, three MIDI zones, and control of Yamaha’s SEQTRAK. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a browser, and has a build for the SMK-37 Elite.

firmwares.title: PaperLagoon
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient firmware: FM voices through a tape echo and a plate play by themselves in seven imaginary worlds, while a key offers something to a hidden state and the knobs change the weather. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Patchwerk
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A modular synth of over 80 modules, among them synth engines, filters, drums, a sampler and granular player, sequencers, and effects, patched and played on the FM1 itself. It installs from its own browser page, whose emulator runs the same firmware with a visual patch bay and can control an FM1 over USB, changes syncing both ways.

firmwares.title: Penumbra
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A space-drone instrument by Lunar Eclipse Forge: five slowly beating voices swell in when it starts, with a soft voice in a long shimmer reverb, a slow swell, a looper that follows the scene's key, and a MORPH control that moves between scenes. Version 1.5 adds a journey that travels by itself, a voice that sings, and loops built from several sounds. It aims for the cinematic drone of the ELTA Solar 42, and installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: PERF-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock).
firmwares.blurb: A live-performance firmware of ten genres of self-playing music that you steer in real time, with an auto-DJ, a drum sequencer, an acid line that answers itself, and a six-operator FM engine that plays 22 DX7-style voices and up to 16 of your own, loaded from a .syx file. It installs from its own browser page, which checks the package against the unit, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: PHREAK
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox on SLOOP, with three synth tracks and three drum tracks whose kits come from a USB stick. Its release carries a firmware package, installed from a computer over USB, and a web installer. Its README calls it a personal fork tested on one FM1, and says it keeps your projects, presets, samples and settings and can go back to SLOOP or the official firmware.

firmwares.title: Pianola
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A player grand piano, called Clair Piano before 1.1: a concert grand modelled from its strings, soundboard, and dampers, on which tapping any key plays the next notes of one of 87 classical piano rolls at your touch, with a plain 27-key piano, a one-finger chord mode, and four user piano rolls. It supports both FM1 flash chips and installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: picovave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: Firmware that runs PICO-8 carts (through the femto8 engine) on the FM1 and the SMK-37 Pro, with the controls mapped to the game pad. It installs from the picovave-fm1.fwsc package in its release, and carts are uploaded over SysEx. Its README is mostly about the SMK-37 Pro and does not state whether it has been tried on an FM1.

firmwares.title: PIGEON
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A performance sampler built on Felucca: two long-song slots with up to 32 playable chops each, and a separate drum kit, sharing 500 KiB of sample storage. It samples digital USB audio straight onto the selected song or drum pad, by threshold or timed capture, and lets you audition and trim a take before keeping it. A browser editor sets each chop's playback points, reverse, cents, gain, and crossfade, and keeps reusable chop collections. A variable-length sequencer has step-grid and piano-roll views, with patterns and an arrangement. It installs from its own browser page, which covers coming from other custom firmware, and its emulator lets you try it first, record WAV or MP3, and send sample banks and sessions to the FM1. This is the final beta: back up a complete session before updating, since v0.3.1 cannot open v0.4 or v0.5 projects.

firmwares.title: PING OS-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-track rhythm synthesis groovebox: 49 synthesised drum models and 20 synths, a sampler and granular engine, 23 effects, parameter locks, a line generator, and an autopilot that keeps varying a pattern. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it, and comes as a VST3 plug-in too.

firmwares.title: Pink Trombone
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A voice synthesiser built on the Pink Trombone vocal tract model, as fm1-dock with the trombone as its only synth, so USB, the installers and the rescue keep working. It installs from the pinktrombone-0.1.fwsc package in its release.

firmwares.title: Piterfly
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing. Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: An alternative OS built on SLOOP and Felucca. Since 1.2.0 tracks 1 to 6 are synth parts sharing eight voices and tracks 7 and 8 are two independent 16-lane drum parts, with eight named song slots, kick ducking chosen part by part, a live granular insert, and MIDI thru on each track. Its release notes say full testing of 1.2.0 on a physical FM1 is still pending. It installs from its own browser page, with a browser editor.

firmwares.title: PLAYA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A performance firmware built on Optimist: two synth layers on one keyboard, layered, split, blended, or alone, with drums on a simple step sequencer, send effects, Bluetooth MIDI keyboards, and one screen whose four knobs edit every parameter, from five engines, 32 drum kits, and 135 presets. Its README says it has been played on one FM1. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page with Optimist's tools or web installer.

firmwares.title: Plissken
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A John Carpenter-inspired soundtrack sketch: the keyboard plays Juno, piano, Pro-1, guitar, bass, CS-50 and CS-80-style sounds, chords, and Linn LM-1 drum samples, with an arpeggiator, a phrase recorder, and a five-track visual sequencer that saves up to 16 songs. Its maker calls it a prototype and says it has been played on an FM1. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page, following the Firmware Hub's install steps with a bootloader.

firmwares.title: Pocket Band
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Writes music with you: pick a place on a map of genre towns and it writes a four-piece sketch of drums, bass, keys, and lead, then re-roll any member, change the key, let the band jam, play punch-in effects, edit any part step by step, and keep four save slots. Its README says 0.2 ran on an FM1, and what 0.3 and 0.4 add has been tested only on a computer. It installs from an installer page in its release.

firmwares.title: Polly
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A pocket arranger in the spirit of the Yamaha QY70: a style plays a band of eight instruments and the chords you play steer it, with songs made of sections, two melodies, and General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, so MIDI in plays it as a sound module too. If you own a QY70, it can build that machine’s 128 preset styles from your own ROM; nothing of Yamaha’s comes with it. Built on Felucca’s platform layer, it installs, teaches, and plays in a browser from its own page.

firmwares.title: POLY5
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Five synths in one on Dinghy: every note goes to the next synth or to a random one, with unison and poly modes too, worn tape, wow and flutter, 24 factory patches each with its own sequence, an arpeggiator, and a step sequencer. Its README says it was tested on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, and its site plays it in a browser.

firmwares.title: POND
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative garden pond derived from AMB-1: switched on, it is already playing breathing voices, drops on loops of unequal length, a gliding bass, and quiet drips through a tape echo and a plate, and you tend it through rain and thunder, across nine pieces. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: PROPHET 67
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A seven-voice analogue-style polysynth, by SIX MACHINES’ maker, after the Sequential Prophet-6: its voice architecture, POLY MOD, VINTAGE character, effects, and knob-per-function workflow, with a manual in German. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Prysm
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-voice wavetable FM synthesizer built on Dinghy and Felucca: two oscillators a voice, each a chain of three wavetable operators that modulate by FM, ring, or mix, with a resonant filter, an LFO, a looping modulation envelope, chorus, delay, plate reverb, and eight patch slots. It installs from its own browser page, which since 0.8 also has an editor that plays Prysm in the page and stays in step with a connected FM1. Version 0.9 added a polyphonic sequencer that records live, and 1.0 VCA OPEN, which holds the amp open for a drone.

firmwares.title: PT/FM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: Pocket Tracker / Fusion Machine, a ProTracker-style tracker whose tracks play synth engines and samples side by side. It installs from the install page in its release, with a demo disk, and has a browser emulator, manual and editor. The README says the firmware runs on the FM1 and is still being made lighter.

firmwares.title: Pulhra
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A hard fork of Felucca: a minimal groovebox with an Elektron-style sequencer and several sound engines. Its release carries the package, an installer page, and an editor, and records a hardware-tested baseline. Its notes report USB audio crackling on the regular firmware, which is under investigation, and advise backing up your banks first.

firmwares.title: PurpleMonkey FM-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A first instrument for a small child, by ChoralRoot's author: press any key and something nice happens. Every key is a note on a five-note scale or a drum, over a backing beat, with four animal friends on the screen and no menus. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: P-Vox
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Polivoks-style firmware by FORM’s maker: two generators, a two-op-amp filter, Bass Support, a sequencer that transposes from the keys, a drum generator with 12-pattern packs for house, dubstep, drum and bass, and techno, and effects on the second core. It installs from its release package, or from the flash page in the same release.

firmwares.title: QUADRO
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-section performance synthesiser after the ARP Quadra: a bass, a string ensemble, a polyphonic synth and a two-voice lead play at once across a split keyboard, through a 14-stage phase shifter, reverb and delay. It has one-finger chords with a bass root, and a sequencer over the keys you hold that syncs to MIDI clock. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Quantum GammaWave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A synth firmware with a wavetable sound, a spectrogram filter, a four-track tape deck, and a song generator with 49 genres, made as a companion to the GammaWave VST. It installs from its own browser page and has a web studio and a browser emulator. Its numbering started again at 1.0 on 16 Nov, after 4.1.0, and its releases of 23 Nov are numbered 1.8, after 1.12.18.

firmwares.title: Quartet
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A four-track groovebox that plays like a four-piece band, lead, pads, bass, and drums. Since 3.1 it has 84 sounds and 26 drum kits, 40 effect pedals with four slots an instrument, a step recorder, beat repeat, a key lock, and a song sequencer in which each instrument follows its own arrangement. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page and plays in fm1-emu in a browser.

firmwares.title: QUARTZ
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-track groovebox on fm1-base, with Plaits' 24 models, a 16-pad kit, a step sequencer with parameter locks and trig conditions, eight generative sources such as Game of Life, chord progressions, and Tonnetz walks, punch-in effects, and an animated scene on every page. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: Quasar
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Firmware after SOMA Laboratory’s Pulsar-23, for experimental IDM, with an audio engine written from scratch: six tracks, 16 engine profiles, 147 sound families, macros, a phrase generator with polymeters, and a performance mode. It installs from its own browser page, which its README says to open in desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera, and the site carries a manual.

firmwares.title: Quod
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone instrument of thirteen sine voices that flow towards the note you play, an angel cluster above the root and a demon cluster below it, with a Heaven / Hell knob. It also runs on a Mac as an Audio Unit instrument, and its FM1 firmware is in its release package.

firmwares.title: Quorum
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A self-playing additive instrument for generative, evolving soundscapes by Arcturus S6’s maker, in which cellular automata decide which harmonics sound. Built on Dinghy; its README says it was tested on one FM1 and calls it experimental. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Rainbow mode
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A music toy for small children, built on Felucca: every key shows its note in its own colour, and 40 friends, from ducks to a unicorn, each bring a picture, a sound, and a beat, with sound tricks on the top buttons and a volume limit for small ears. Holding HOME and SAVE opens the full Felucca synth. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE's V15 back, and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: RAKT
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generates a band in one press: chords, bass, drums, and melody in a chosen style stay in sync and play off each other, and in GLO Live the keys solo parts, cue fills and drops, and play effects. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: RAMBEAVER
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A side-scrolling action game: defend the dam, ride through robot city, fly to the data center, and defeat Mother. It comes as a firmware package with a quick-start guide, installed with the tools in its source archive.

firmwares.title: RAVE FM 2
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: An early hardcore groovebox of six tracks: kick, break, 909, bass, lead, and stab or hoover, with hardcore kick presets, sliced breakbeats, a song mode, sidechain on every track, and live effects on the keys such as risers, drops, and rolls. Built on Felucca and JIANT FM, it installs from its release package and has a manual.

firmwares.title: Ravel
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A pocket groovebox of eight tracks for sound design, with a shared tape that the tracks catch, cut up, and rebuild. Its README says it runs on the FM1 and in a browser emulator. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: RDPNO
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Roland’s SA pianos, from the MKS-20 and the Rhodes MK-80, through rdpiano’s emulation of their board, ported to Dinghy and playing up to eight notes. No Roland data is included: its browser page installs the firmware with your own ROM dumps, and has an editor.

firmwares.title: RED MASS VAMPIRE OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: Six tracks, five instruments and drums, with 256 built-in sounds, two trap kits, 64 steps a track, and a song mode. Its release carries a firmware package and a Windows installer, and its README says booting and running it on an FM1 still need checking.

firmwares.title: REDACTED
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental four-track lo-fi groovebox built on Felucca: ALGORITHM picks the track, and four knobs set its fracture, static, chance, and mutate. It installs from its own browser page, which offers 0.1 as a known-working rollback because hardware testing of 0.2 is still pending.

firmwares.title: RemoteFM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware that does almost nothing by itself: it sends every key, button, encoder and the MASTER pot to a computer and shows what the computer sends back on its LEDs and screen, so a firmware built for an emulator runs on the computer with the FM1 as its panel. It installs from its own browser page, and its release has packages with and without Bluetooth MIDI.

firmwares.title: ReVo
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental soundscape instrument with two machines: Bioma, a synthesised ecosystem of birds, insects and water, and Atolls, two sample loops you steer with windows, fragments and landing points. A browser editor writes samples to its four device slots. Built on Felucca and SLOOP. It installs from its own browser page, which checks the package’s identity and hash.

firmwares.title: ReplicantFM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An acid, techno and big-beat groovebox forked from Felucca, with a drum machine modelled on the TR-909, a mono synth modelled on the SH-101, two TB-303-style basslines with an algorithmic generator, and a sliced breakbeat player that takes your own loops. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE’s firmware back, and has a manual.

firmwares.title: RhinoTiger
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative psytrance firmware, from dark psy to hi-tech, that plays by itself while you steer it: a kick, a rolling FM bass, percussion, a repeating line, one-shot sounds, and a held atmosphere on a grid of sixteenths, in eight worlds, with four macro knobs, a mix with mutes, and an auto play that plays a whole set. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser, and has manuals in English and Japanese.

firmwares.title: Rhythmer
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox based on JIANT, with nine synth models, 303-style acid and sequenced breakbeats. It installs from its browser installer or its release package, and has a browser emulator and editor. Its README says the owner has confirmed listening on a device, warns that its package restores its factory loops, and says to back up first.

firmwares.title: RHYTM-SEC-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generative drums and bass with PERF-1's drum and bass voices and FMini-1's ladder filter: pick one of 19 styles and it draws patterns from that genre's feel, which keep changing as you play, over a bass line in your key, with breaks, builds, and fills on a button, a DJ filter, MIDI clock, and USB audio stems. It installs from its release package, or as an fm1-dock module, and plays in fm1-emu in a browser.

firmwares.title: RIDDIM ROOTS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative reggae and dub band: six players (drums and percussion, bass, skank, organ, horns and lead, and piano) across 11 styles from ska to dub techno, with an Evolve control and transitions that do not stop the music. Its README, in Ukrainian, says it is built on M-VAVE’s FM1 Open SDK. It has no release; its .fwsc package is in the repository.

firmwares.title: Ripple
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Runs instruments written in Lua over sounds written in Faust or C, copied to the FM1 as a USB drive with nothing to reflash, after monome's norns. Its site plays it in a browser, installs it, and has a manual, and its emulator has a panel for writing your own.

firmwares.title: ROM-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A sixteen-part sound module, as the rack modules of the nineties were: a part for each MIDI channel, each playing a preset of sounds you choose, with a filter, envelopes, reverb, and chorus. It plays .sf2 files. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried in a browser first.

firmwares.title: RudimentSeq
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Felucca fork in which any track can play one of 174 drum rudiments in place of its step pattern, each hand on a note of its own with the sticking's accents, ghost notes, and grace notes, across up to four rudiment lanes. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Ruido
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drone synthesiser of four Schmitt-trigger oscillators, made as a raw stereo source for guitar pedals and modular systems, with three pressure keyboards and an oscilloscope always on the screen. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: RUPTURE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A monophonic bass synth built on Cycle Exchange Synthesis, with a selectable band-limited saw oscillator, two sub-oscillators, modulation, sound shaping, effects, and a sequencer and arpeggiator. Its README says some of its fixes still need confirming on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: S1Vave
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-voice virtual analogue synth after the Roland SH-101 and S-1, with an arpeggiator and a step sequencer. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Saadet
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A synthesiser fork of Melodee, by its author, with Bluetooth MIDI and 24-bit audio.
