Its 1.0 has six engines, among them a PPG Wave and a three-oscillator HYDRA, two parts, factory libraries, and a web editor, and the project also builds for the SMK-37. Its README called 0.1 experimental, with checks of the exact release package still pending. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: SAMSARA
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A slow ambient piece that plays itself and changes over hours, a fork of Charles Vestal's AMB-1: a pad, bells, a gliding bass, and a low ground that come and go like weather, through a tape echo and a plate, with Mood, Density, Drift, and Space on the knobs. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Sardine
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Live club mixing: four layers, lead, chord, bass, and drums, play by themselves in twenty club styles while you drop in new lines, break it down, and blend into the next style. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: SATIE-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: An evolving Satie soundtrack: Gymnopédies 1–3, Gnossiennes 1–3 and Ogives 1–4 in five moods, with lead, bass, an optional inner voice, drums and atmosphere that follow the scores and evolve while you work. Four Home knobs set Tempo, Energy, Evolve and Mix, and GLO opens a built-in guide. They are simplified electronic arrangements, not piano performances. Its notes record installs from V15 and back passing on an FM1, and say recovery from an interrupted update is not yet tested.

firmwares.title: SARDAB
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A dungeon-synth firmware turned toward the desert, built on GHOULBOX (a Felucca fork) with maqam tuning, Arabic rhythms, oud and ney recordings and stone-room reverbs. It installs from its own browser page. The README calls the current build a development preview that has been tested on a host and emulator, with validation on a physical FM1 still pending.

firmwares.title: Scintilla
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: The Elka Synthex of 1981, by fm1-emu's maker, ported from synthex-web and checked sample by sample against it: its 80 factory sounds, two layers of eight voices, chorus, and an algorithmic reverb. Its release notes say the code was installed and played on a real FM1; the delay and saving edited sounds are still to come. It installs from its release package with the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in fm1-emu.

firmwares.title: Selva1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A synth inspired by São Paulo, with three wavetable, analog, FM, or noise oscillators, a ladder filter, a modulation matrix, and a 303-style sequencer. The same engine runs in a browser and as a plugin; the FM1 version is built on SLOOP and installs from its own page. Its notes are in Portuguese.

firmwares.title: SEQ-4
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM-1 into four MIDI sequencers (melody, chords, eight-track drums and two generative modes) for controlling other instruments; the FM-1 makes no sound of its own. Its 1.0 release is the first marked as ready for everyday use, and its README reports timing measured on an FM-1. It installs from its own browser page in Chrome or Edge, and also from its release package, with a browser emulator to try first.

firmwares.title: SHIFL
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A live groovebox firmware based on Felucca, with six synth tracks and a drum machine, a song mode, USB audio, MIDI clock and a full backup. It installs from its own browser page, which also has an editor and a way back to the official firmware. Its README calls it a beta and says to install at your own risk. Its one GitHub release, 1.0.0, packages it for the Firmware Hub, while its README names the version 3.0.

firmwares.title: Shine On
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A seventies string machine built from OberVave: six fixed registers from contrabass to horn, three bucket-brigade lines for the ensemble, a phaser, delay, and plate reverb, 16 voices, an arpeggiator, and a two-track sequencer. Its README says it has been tested on an FM1. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package.

firmwares.title: SHRUB
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A wavetable synth from the maker of Serum, with Serum's wavetables, filters, and envelopes, LFOs, a 16-slot modulation matrix, a seven-effect rack, an arpeggiator, an eight-lane motion sequencer, and 100 factory presets. It installs from its own browser page, and its browser editor edits the FM1 over USB or plays SHRUB without one.

firmwares.title: SID-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: Two Commodore 64 SID chips as a six-voice synth, from a port of reSID, with the 6581 or the 8580 and a library of 128 patches. Its web app edits them, takes the instruments and drums out of a .sid tune, and plays the tune on the FM1 over MIDI. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: SiDJ
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A C64 music deck that plays High Voltage SID Collection tunes on an emulated C64, with every voice open to remixing from the panel or a MIDI keyboard. It sounds through the FM1's audio jack, over USB audio with each voice on its own channel, or on real SID hardware over ASID. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: SIDOU
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock). Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A C64 SID tracker-synth: two SIDs, a drum kit made on the chip's own voices and four sampled digi drums, steps given a chance to play, songs written on the FM1's keys that open in GoatTracker 2, and MIDI clock and SysEx. Its 0.2.0 test build ran on one FM1 before 0.3.0. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Sill
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generative 90s eurodance: press PLAY and it writes a song in one of ten styles, with offbeat basses, piano and supersaw stabs, a hook, a choir, and a key change for the last chorus, steered with four knobs. It is built on Daurade, Tuna and Felucca. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried in a browser first. It runs on the FM-1, with no warranty.

firmwares.title: Sillage
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track groovebox derived from Skiff and Felucca, with its notes in French: 448 presets, a sequencer, a song mode, scenes and a PERFORM mode, a live mixer, and a USB editor. Its README says the firmware was validated on a physical FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it, and its release carries the package.

firmwares.title: SIREN
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A rave that writes itself, a firmware made from Clipper and SLOOP. Its README calls 0.10 experimental: it passes its tests on a computer and is being tested on the FM1. It installs from its browser installer, with SIREN STUDIO beside it, and can go back to V16 or V15.

firmwares.title: SIX MACHINES
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing.
firmwares.blurb: A performance drum machine in the spirit of the Elektron boxes and the Erica Synths LXR-02, on fm1-base: six synthesised drum machines whose knobs are macros resting on named sweet spots. While it plays it sends MIDI clock and its kick’s hits over USB, to lead a computer or another FM1. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: Skiff
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox built on Felucca, whose engines, sounds, and file formats it keeps: fourteen synth and drum engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions, and parameter locks, patterns and songs, a performance layer, and screens that draw what each knob does. It installs from its own browser page, which can also return the FM1 to M-VAVE’s V15, and it has a browser editor. Version 2.0 adds a new sequencer and songs that chain, 2.0.1 also has builds for the SMK-37 Pro keyboard, and 2.6 shows the FM1’s screen, large, in the editor’s Screen tab.

firmwares.title: Skiff Atlatl
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Skiff's groovebox with more engines: wavetable, additive, a Moog-style oscillator, and a Plaits port, with analogue-modelled filters, Devilfish-style controls, a step arpeggiator, eight tracks of USB audio for a DAW, and screen mirroring. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: SLOOP
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox firmware built on Felucca, with projects, patterns, and songs, twelve engines, among them a six-operator FM that imports DX7 voices and physical models of strings and bells, and its own web editor for presets and a sound library. It installs from its own browser page and leaves through M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE, as Felucca does.

firmwares.title: SLOOP ALG
firmwares.status: Test build · Latest ALG05 Updated 7 Oct 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental fork of SLOOP 2.2 that adds engines of its own: a six-operator DX7 that imports DX7 voices, virtual analogue, additive, pluck, and Karplus-Strong strings, each editable on the FM1. It installs from its own browser page and has its own web editor for sounds. Its notes are in Chinese.

firmwares.title: SLOOP Dub
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP with a dub wing: a DUB filter module, a dub siren on OCT+, ten riddims to load into the sequencer, a four-band isolator, a tape delay whose TIME knob bends the loop, per-track throws, and a WIRES visualiser. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: SLOOP DX7 Banks
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in its editor, and presets grouped by kind. Its builds are tests, so back up first. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: SLOOP Floyd FM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP with a four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an envelope per operator, seven pages, and a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub.

firmwares.title: sloopDX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: SLOOP's live workflow with a DX7 inside: a fork of SLOOP that replaces its engines with one six-operator DX7 engine, ported from Dexed, with every voice parameter editable on the FM1 and room for 256 voices from your own banks. Its drum track plays FM drums you program on the device, and patterns run up to 128 steps. It installs from its own browser page and has its own web editor.

firmwares.title: Smileyface
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: You’re making Acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! A truly trippy experience, as faithful to the 303 Devil Fish and the TD-3-MO as it can be. Built on Chipbox.

firmwares.title: Solinaesque
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A paraphonic divide-down string machine with 16′, 8′, and 4′ registers, one filter and envelope for every note, a three-phase ensemble, a flanger, a delay, an arpeggiator, and chord memory. Its README says it runs on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: SPAMPY
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A custom firmware based on Felucca and Sloop, with a synthwave-inspired interface, sound tools, scenes, drum processing, effects, and games. Its 1.0 release adds Neon arpeggiator modes, a slicer, an extended envelope, and five built-in arcade games. It installs from its release package, and has a video guide.

firmwares.title: Speak37
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A talking synth, written for the SMK-37 and built for the FM1 too: every key speaks the next word at its pitch, chords speak in harmony, and MOPE, a gloomy robot, says what he thinks of what you play. Its README asks for feedback on how it plays on the FM1. It installs from the SMK37 page’s FM-1 tab.

firmwares.title: SPELLBOX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: A talking spelling game after the 1978 Speak & Spell, written independently with its own speech, built on foma. It has SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE and MYSTERY WORD games on four levels, a SING mode, a letter synth on the keys, and circuit-bending settings. It installs from its own browser page, which can also restore the original firmware. Its README is in French.

firmwares.title: SPIRALFM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-track live groovebox built on Mycelium and SLOOP, with six psytrance, techno, and acid grooves, four 240-bar factory songs, a PSY FX page, and per-track probability. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: SPLITMILK
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Splits the keyboard in two: the lower keys play one instrument, CHOC, and the upper keys another, BERRY, each with its own sound, octave, volume, and playing mode, with a drum machine and a pad sequencer beside them. It installs from its release package with M-Flasher.

firmwares.title: SQ-80
firmwares.hubUsefulness: SysEx / DX7 .syx transfer capable (needs Hub SysEx unlock).
firmwares.blurb: An Ensoniq SQ-80 and ESQ-1 engine written from scratch on fm1-base, playing ESQ-1 and SQ-80 SysEx patches with waves read from your own ROM dumps; no Ensoniq ROM data is included. Its README says it runs on an FM1, and on a Donner Starrykey 37 Play with its SMK-37 build. It installs from its own browser page or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and has a manual and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: SQRL-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Felucca with a shell of its own, built around pairs: a SOUND that makes the tone (FM6, LIZARD, SHOCK, DRUMS, MOUTH, ANALOG, PHASE, or PHYS) and a NOTE engine that chooses the notes (KEYS, CHORD, RUDIMENT, LINES, ALIVE, and more). Hold HOME and the octave becomes a wheel for picking the pair. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Stack Trace CFW
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware built on M-VAVE’s FM1 Open V14 that adds four engines, a virtual analogue polysynth, a TR-909, a C64 SID, and a granular one, with a 128-step sequencer with Euclidean and 303 acid generators, an eight-scene clip launcher, grit and punch effects, a sample slicer, MIDI CC learn, and four demo songs. It installs from its release package with M-VAVE’s FM-1 Workbench.

firmwares.title: Stallion
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A synthesiser grown out of Clipper, SLOOP, and Felucca, for the FM1 and the SMK-37 Pro, with 26 engines, four of them new, and 819 factory sounds. Its README says it is built on Clipper 1.3, which runs on the FM1, and passes its test suite on a computer, and that its SMK-37 build has been played on an SMK-37 Pro. It installs from its own browser page, with a web editor.

firmwares.title: Stamp Composer
firmwares.hubUsefulness: MIDI Out / external hardware sequencing. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A Mario Paint-style music composer: stamp characters on a staff to write songs with 31 Mario Paint sounds, eight layers, flats and triplets, swing, and bar editing. It has per-sound MIDI out, clock sync, eight song slots with autosave, and a Twinkle Twinkle demo song, and installs from its own page. The sounds and sprites come from Super Mario Paint, a separate asset pack with its own notice.

firmwares.title: STRANGER SYNTH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A performance synth in the spirit of 1980s analogue film scores, based on OFFWORLD: walls of detuned saws, an arpeggiator that follows MIDI clock, chords from one finger, a sidechain, and eight performance effects, with a second FM1 running SIX MACHINES as its drummer. It installs from its release package, plays in a browser, and has manuals in English and German.

firmwares.title: Switch Blade
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Four synth machines on Felucca, one per track with eight voices shared: OB-Z, a brassy poly; WAVE, from Void Wave; NANO, a 303 and a polysynth; and JUNO, with a Juno-60-style chorus. It has no drums, as a synth expansion played over MIDI, and installs from its own page.

firmwares.title: SY1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A polysynth by NCC’s maker that plays Synth1 patches (.sy1), with Synth1’s 99 parameters under its own numbers: two oscillators and a sub, FM, ring and sync, filters, three envelopes, two LFOs, an arpeggiator, unison, and effects, with 256 community presets built in and a bitimbral mode on the FM1’s second core. Its README says it installs and runs on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser first, and has a patch manager.

firmwares.title: Synthesthetic
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An audio-visual instrument with 30 audio-reactive visualisers on the FM1's screen and over USB as a webcam. Its release notes say 0.2 has been tested on one FM1, with macOS only. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser version plays it first.

firmwares.title: SynthMaven
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O.
firmwares.blurb: A Melodee-based groovebox for oriental live music, with a song arranger of up to 16 sections and engines such as DX7, Juno, and acid beside Melodee's own. It installs from its own browser page and has a web editor and an illustrated guide.

firmwares.title: Tack
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A digital drum synth with seven voices and a step sequencer, using the LXR-02 firmware's sound engine, in two forms: firmware for the FM1 and CLAP, VST3 and Audio Unit plugins for a DAW. It is licensed GPL-3.0, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Tangram
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative MIDI sequencer and composer for Berlin School, ambient, and minimal music: voices play patterns of different lengths that shift against each other, with a multi-stage Composer, a MIDI delay, and drums. It makes no sound of its own and plays other instruments over MIDI. Its README lists its sequencing, Composer, and drums as used on hardware. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: TastyWaves
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A twelve-voice wavetable synthesiser built on Dinghy, with two oscillators per voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, a four-slot effects chain, an arpeggiator, and two step sequencers. A browser tool manages patches and loads your own wavetables, and its README says it was tested on an FM1.

firmwares.title: Tekstuur
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An instrument for long, slowly moving sound, by Golf's maker: four layers each play a built-in or sent recording as loops, grains, a stretched freeze, or ringing strings, mixed by a vector point that Evolve moves by itself, through chorus, delay, and a reverb with shimmer and freeze. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Telegram 101
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A 101 lead, a Dillo acid bass, and an 808 drum machine together on the keys, by BB1’s maker. It installs from its own browser page, and has a player guide.

firmwares.title: Tessera
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative firmware for composing through systems, called Melodee (Tess) before 2.0. Each of its four tracks plays its own steps or one of thirteen generators, among them Turing, Euclid, Markov, Atlas, and Chord, or one seeded from a phrase played on the keys. Tracks follow and answer each other in one harmony, 16 mod cords connect anything to anything, and sections and a shape for the whole piece let a project unfold over minutes or hours. It installs from its own browser page, in Chrome or Edge, which can also put M-VAVE’s firmware back.

firmwares.title: Tether
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns an FM1 into the front panel of FM1.Pocket, a browser emulator of the FM1: its keys, knobs, and buttons play the page, and the page’s screen and lights show on the unit. With no page open it works as a USB MIDI controller. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Textura
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A texture synthesiser for the sounds of nature, rain, streams, fire, wind, insects, and birds, computed live with no samples. Four lanes play at once, each a cloud of small events whose number and activity are set from the keys. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: THEORY-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Lessons, quizzes, and a chord lab for music theory, from scales and modes to chords and keys, in English, Italian, Spanish, and German. It installs from its release package, and its README says it is not yet tested on every unit.

firmwares.title: TheReFmB1rth
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A four-machine acid groovebox: two 303-style mono synths, an 808, and a 909, with patterns, song chaining, and performance effects. Its notes record test passes on an FM1, and it has no licence file. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Tidepool
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient loop instrument with twelve synthesised scenes that play by themselves, and a Blank Canvas for recording your own loops. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried first in a browser.

firmwares.title: Timer Tom
firmwares.status: Beta · No numbered releases Updated 26 Nov 2026
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Four kitchen timers, set with K1–K4, each with one of twelve dish icons. While they run, each adds a layer of a soft ambient-techno groove, each key starts a slow melodic loop, and the key lights run like an hourglass. Its README calls 0.1 a beta, tested on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE’s V15 back.

firmwares.title: TONIC
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A Digitone-style FM groovebox with four-operator FM, virtual analogue, and drum engines, twelve voices, and a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks. Its README says it runs on an FM1, though its 0.12 release notes say it has not yet been tested on a physical one. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first.

firmwares.title: Tonitor
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Electroacoustic firmware for experimentation, live ambient music, and sound exploration, and not a groovebox. Six layers each take an FM, ANIMA, CALIGULA or RUSSOLO engine and generate their own sounds, with a looper, filter, granulator, bit crusher, and plate reverb on each. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: Tono
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generative ambient firmware built on JIANT FM, Felucca, and fm1-amb: four layers share an instrument engine, each with its own sounds, modulation, effects, and sequencing, steered through the piece with one knob, with displays that answer the music. It installs from its release package through FM-SWITCH, and plays in a browser and in a macOS emulator.

firmwares.title: TransitFM1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A tiny firmware, by ChoralRoot's maker, to stop at between two others: it makes no sound and stores nothing, answers installers as M-VAVE's V15, and carries ChoralRoot's flash safeguards, so an install cut off part way brings the FM1 back in update mode. Its README says 0.1 worked on an FM1, and 0.1.1 fixed two bugs seen on one. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

firmwares.title: TRAPSTATION OS
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A trap and phonk groovebox forked from BBL JAM BOX: six tracks with 808s, FM keys, bells, and pads, generators for drums, hats, chords, and bass, a sampler with slices, a piano roll, a performance page with mutes, effect throws, and bar jumps, and tape, VHS, and vinyl colour on the master. It installs from its own browser page, and has a cheat sheet.

firmwares.title: TRIBE
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A ten-track groovebox built on X0X in which any engine plays on any track: two kicks, the 909 and 808 voices, a 303, and ACID, LEAD, FM4, and NOISE engines, with sixty-four clips a track since 0.3 and a song mode that plays them in turn, scatter effects on the keys, two master effects every track sends to, and four master knobs you assign. Its page installs it from Chrome or Edge, can put the stock firmware back, and plays it in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Trireme
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Turns the FM1 into a macro keyboard that VIAL configures, keeping its settings in flash. It stays a USB MIDI device, so the usual firmware installers still reach it. It installs from its release package.

firmwares.title: Trumpagotchi
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Standalone game/demo; Hub MIDI sequencing N/A.
firmwares.blurb: An unofficial parody virtual pet: feed him burgers, praise him, and put him to bed, and when he is happy he plays bongos on the pentatonic keyboard. It is installed with a Python tool from the release's .fwsc package.

firmwares.title: Tuna
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Generative music built on Felucca: randomness after Mutable Instruments' Marbles, shaped into melody, bass, accompaniment, and percussion in a chosen composer's manner or one of 86 genres from the 1950s to now. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

firmwares.title: Typhoon
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware for playing the FM1 from an EWI wind controller, with a preset editor and a simulator in the browser. Its README calls it an early alpha whose controls are still changing, and it installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: U0U
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A drum machine of nine synthesised kits with no samples: the white keys are the steps and the black keys the drums, every effect on the master bus has 16 steps of its own, and patterns chain into a song, with per-step timing, roll, chance, and pitch, two LFOs, Euclidean rhythms, and MIDI clock over USB. Its README says it has been used on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it.

firmwares.title: Unholy Union
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: Generative ambient and drone, built on Felucca and Jangada: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence, and a chord arpeggio under a voice you play. It installs from its own browser page, which keeps saved projects.

firmwares.title: Vallée
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A moodbox built on Skiff that writes a song, or helps you write one from chords you play, then lets you perform it with each key a part of the song, a being summoned to improvise in your chords, and a retro colour engine on the mix. Since 1.0 its synth engines, sounds, and drum kits are SPAMPY’s. It installs from its own browser page, with an editor and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: Veffbox
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A resampling sound-design instrument: pick a source (FM, analogue, drums, or a resample), play it, modulate it with six LFOs and three envelopes, stack up to eight effects, then resample, and every resample keeps its recipe. Its README says 0.4.0 runs on the FM1. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: VESPER
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An ambient worship firmware with 16 scenes, each stacking four pad-like voices in a chosen major key, plus a global effects chain. It installs from the installer page in its release, or from the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and can be tried in a browser. GitHub lists no licence; the README describes its own code as GPL-3.0 with the FM1 SDK linking exception.

firmwares.title: VIBE FM Link
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Makes the FM1 a controller for the VIBE FM, its web player and its VST, or for anything else that takes MIDI: the keys play, the knobs and buttons send the VIBE’s controls, and the FM1 makes no sound of its own. Built on Dinghy, it installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub or its release package, which has builds for the SMK-37 too.

firmwares.title: Viber
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track groovebox for the FM1 and the SMK-37 Pro, based on Skiff and Felucca: synths and drums, a wavetable engine, a clips mode on two pages, and a screen that shows what each control does. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put the official firmware back, and has an editor and a browser emulator.

firmwares.title: VIRGO
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A gravitational-wave synthesiser by Mario Texture, sister of Grana: every note is a black-hole merger, with four events at once, a detector you tune like a radio, and a long reverb with shimmer. It installs through an editor page in its release, which also simulates it, and has a Bluetooth variant. Its interface is in Italian.

firmwares.title: VNL-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative lo-fi hip hop groovebox on fm1-base, with a sample bank of piano, guitars, cello, harp, and room kits. It installs from its own browser page, which offers the sample bank after the firmware, and its notes say it runs on FM1s with either flash chip.

firmwares.title: Volna
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A wavetable synth with three oscillators a voice, two filters, four envelopes, a modulation matrix, effects, and a step arpeggiator that keeps its own pattern in each patch. It installs from its own browser page, whose editor also manages patches and four user wavetables. Its notes say to back up before changing firmware.

firmwares.title: WaveLoop FM-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: four track faders, knobs that follow the track, preset and engine browsing, a master DJ filter, momentary effect pads, and the session picked up where you left it. It installs from its own browser page.

firmwares.title: White Rabbit
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: An eight-track tracker with patterns of up to 64 steps on the FM1, and synths for six-operator FM with 32 algorithms, detuned analogue-style oscillators with a resonant filter, and chiptune voices. It has 58 synth presets and 27 performance effects, such as repeat, reverse, and dub echo, which can be latched live and recorded into a pattern. Its sampler is not available on the FM1. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser too.

firmwares.title: winampFM
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A firmware in the style of Winamp 2, based on SLOOP 2.8.4: sounds become a playlist, four tracks record as loops, effects sit on sliders, and 28 visualisers fill the screen. It installs from its own page, which runs it in a 3D simulator first. Its numbering now follows No Man Sky FM, so 0.9 comes after 0.12.

firmwares.title: X0X
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A groovebox in the spirit of ReBirth: a 909, an 808, two 303s with an acid line generator, and a breakbeat player, all playing at once, with automation, shared reverb and tape delay sends, and a master compressor. A fork of Felucca, it installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back.

firmwares.title: X0X Extended Edition
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of X0X that keeps its 909, 808, two 303s, and breakbeat player and adds song blocks and variations, per-sound filters and limiters, and finer timing divisions. Sequences copy whole or one part at a time, any single drum row or either 303, keeping the destination's accents and swing, and each paste can be undone. Tested on only one FM1 so far.

firmwares.title: X0X Live
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of X0X built for playing live: two 303s and generative 909 and 808 kits on one LIVE screen, with phrases to generate, keep, and develop, a Director that queues the next intro, break, or drop, a mixer with mutes and solo, and momentary effects such as filters, tape stop, and snare rolls. It installs from its own browser page, with a browser emulator to try first. Hardware testing is still pending.

firmwares.title: X0X-RMX
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of X0X that adds a remix engine with 256 step-remapping patterns for the 909, 808, and both 303s, a TB-3PO generator with 22 scales and motif-based basslines, Grids pattern generation, and an experimental 303 Morph waveform, with pattern chaining, saved startup patterns, and custom LCD colours. It installs from its own browser page, with a browser emulator to try first.

firmwares.title: XENOLITH
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: An experimental FM synthesiser of up to 64 paired oscillator cells, joined in parallel, in series, in branches, and with feedback, with up to eight-note paraphony, sequencing, a multimode filter, a wavefolder, and reverb. It installs from its release package or with a Windows updater, whose install path its README says was exercised on a connected FM1.

firmwares.title: XMOD
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A MOD and XM tracker that plays and edits FastTracker 2 and ProTracker songs on the FM1, with up to 32 channels, and a browser song manager for moving .xm and .mod files. It installs from its release package (xmod.fwsc) with any FM1 installer, and has a browser simulator. The README says it is not tested on V16.

firmwares.title: Yanfei
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Multi-track song/pattern chaining fits Section 2B.
firmwares.blurb: A fork of Felucca with twelve engines, 96 factory presets and a four-track tracker. It installs from the browser installer on its own website, which also has an editor and an emulator. It has no GitHub releases, and its README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.

firmwares.title: Yehnah
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A six-track synth, drum machine and song sequencer built on JIANT FM, with 25 synthesis engines and over 700 sounds, a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, songs of sections and scenes, one-key chords, and IDEAS, which writes a pattern, sound or effect for the track. It installs from the browser, where an editor and an emulator of the firmware also run. Its README asks for official V15 before installing.

firmwares.title: ZEN-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Ambient firmware that plays itself: a cherry tree dropping petals on a river, koi in a pond, and fireflies over a stream, where every movement on screen is a note. The keys and knobs play along, and it installs from its own web page, which can put M-VAVE's firmware back, with a browser emulator to try first.

firmwares.title: ZENITH-1
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: A generative ambient machine built on AMB-1 that plays itself from the moment it is switched on: pads, bells on tape loops of unequal lengths, a bass, soft percussion, and now and then a lead, travelling through eight worlds. 27 effects sit on the keys, which can also strum or play the lead. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser.

firmwares.title: Zodiac
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Play/sequence via Hub Ch 1 MIDI In + --map panel/knobs.
firmwares.blurb: Twelve signs of the zodiac, each a moving picture and a piece of ambient music that plays itself, handing over to the next sign every 30 minutes. Its site installs it and plays it in a browser.

firmwares.title: zp12
firmwares.hubUsefulness: Has browser editor for patch/sample/project I/O. Imports/exports patterns, banks, or presets.
firmwares.blurb: A 12-bit sampling drum machine in the spirit of the 80s: 32 pads at 26 kHz, pitched with no interpolation, eight filtered channels on the knobs, eleven loops on the black keys, songs, step editing, swing, and sloopDX's effects. A fork of SLOOP on sloopDX's platform, it saves beside sloopDX's banks without touching them, and takes your own samples from a browser editor, or since 2.5 records them on the FM1 over USB. It installs from its own browser page.
